Be turned white. Hafakh lavon means be turned white.
Be deeper. Its depth is deeper than the depth of the skin. The word amok (deep) does not mean the same as shafal (lower) (v. 20).
And pronounce him unclean. Verbally. He shall declare him unclean.
Then the priest shall shut up him that hath the plague seven days. The person shall be shut up. He shall wait up to seven days, for most illnesses change on the seventh day.

Stay in its appearance. Amad be-enav means stay in its appearance. The term enav is employed, for its appearance is seen by the eye. All the commentaries says that beenav (in its appearance) means in its make-up, that is, in the way it was.
Spread. Pasah means spread.
Again. Shenit (again) means a second time.

The plague be dim. Many of the wise men say that the word kehah (dim) means dark. They offer proof from vatikhhena (were dim) in and his eyes were dim (Bereshit 27:1). They say that the phrase kehot levanot (dull white) (v. 39) is similar to le-vanah adamdamet (reddish-white) (v. 19) in that it contains both colors. However, I believe that the word kehah (dim) is the reverse of pasah (spread). It is related to the word va-tikhhena (were dim) in and his eyes were dim (Bereshit 27:1). The word khihah (stopped) in and he diminished them not (Shmuel I 3:13) is close to it. The meaning of kahah ha-nega (the plague be dim) is that the plague did not spread to another place. Note, there are two signs, namely, the size of the affliction was diminished and it did not spread to the healthy part of the body.
Then the priest shall pronounce him clean. The kohen shall say that he is clean, for it was a scab (mispachat). However, if it spreads afterwards he is unclean.
Then he shall be brought. The man having the affliction. Be brought is to be interpreted like its counterpart.
And it have turned. The black hair white.
Quick. The meaning of michyat (quick) is live flesh. Flesh which does not feel is not alive.
Old. Of yore.
Yasgirennu (shut him up) governs two actions. It means he shall command that the afflicted be shut up.

He shall pronounce him clean that hath the plague. For the plague has already surfaced and removed itself from the afflicted. The meaning of ve-tiher et hanaga (he shall pronounce him unclean that hath the plague) is that he shall verbally clean the affliction; that is, he shall declare that this plague will not make others unclean.
But if the raw flesh again be turned. For it is possible that the affliction will return.
Reddish-white. A mixture of the two colors. Or a little of each.

The word tzara’at (leprosy) (v. 20) means a disease. Similarly ha-tzirah (the disease) in I will send the disease (Shemot 23:28). The fact that the Torah reads, and I will send is no argument against this interpretation, for Scripture reads, He sent His word (Tehillim 107:20); For I…send all My plagues (Shemot 9:14); and He sent forth upon them the fierceness of His anger (Tehillim 78:49).

And, behold, if the appearance thereof. It is not grammatically correct to vocalize the alef of mareha (its appearance) with a long kamatz and a mappik in the heh as in the case of yadah (her hand) and raglah (her foot), for we do not find words whose roots end in a silent heh to be so treated.

[Look on it.] The nun of yirennah (look upon it) has a dagesh in it like the nun of yasgirennu (v. 11) to compensate for the missing added heh. The same is true with mi-mennah (from her) and mi-mennu (from it).
In its place. If the affliction stays in its place, for there are afflictions that move from place to place.
Scar. The word tzarevet (scar) is similar to the word ve-nitzrevu (shall be seared) in and all faces…shall be seared (Yechezkel 21:30). It has the meaning of a burning mass, heat, and a flame.
Or white. Alone.

And if the bright spot stay in its place…but be dim. The word kehah (dim) is to be understood as I explained it earlier (v. 6). Scripture does not mention kehah (dim) the first time, But if the bright spot stay in its place (v. 23), because there the bright spot remains as it was.

[And when…] Scripture mentions a man or a woman because it deals with an affliction in the beard [and the head]. Also, because the Torah has to use the word ish (man), and not the term adam (a human being) to exclude women from the law of the bald head and the bald forehead (v. 40). Note, our verse means, when a man or a woman has an affliction upon the head or a man upon the beard.
Yellow. The word tzahov (yellow) in Arabic refers to a color that is close to white.
It is a scall. The word netek (scall) is related to the word yennatek (is broken) in as a string of tow is broken (Jud. 16:9). The reference is to the hair.
Then he shall be shaven. The head or the beard shall be shaven. However, the place of the netek (scall) shall not be shaven.
And he shall wash his clothes. It is unnecessary to say that he shall bathe in water.

Shall not seek. The meaning of yevakker is, he shall seek. Similarly u-vikkartim (and seek them out) (Yechezkel 34:11). It is close in meaning to the word separate. Similarly He shall not inquire (yevakker) whether it be good or bad (Vayikra 27:33).
A tetter. The word bohak (tetter) is known in Rabbinic literature. It has no counterpart in Scripture.

Be fallen off. Yimmaret (be fallen off) is similar to moretim (them that plucked off the hair) in And my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair (Is. 50:6). The latter refers to the hair that is around the cheeks.
He is bald. Kere’ach (bald) is similar to korchah (baldness) in nor make any baldness (Devarim 14:1). The meaning of his head is, his entire head.

Forehead-bald. The word gibbe’ach (forehead-bald) has no neighbor except in this section. Gibbe’ach is an adjective. In my opinion kere’ach (bald) refers to the top of the head. Scripture does not mention a woman because a woman does not become bald as she contains a lot of moisture, and hair is similar to grass.
As the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the flesh. On the rest of the body.

His clothes shall be rent. The word perumim means rent. The leper is to be so dressed so that he may be recognized because of his abnormal garb. Or the leper is to behave like a mourner. Scripture therefore states, his clothes shall be rent, and the hair of his head shall go loose. The reason for the latter is so that the leper mourn for his evil actions, for this plague came upon him because of his deeds.
His upper lip. Safam refers to the upper lip. The mem of safam is a root letter. The word sefamo (his beard) in nor trimmed his beard (Shmuel II 19:22) is proof.

And he shall cover. With his garments. The word yateh (he shall cover) is related to the word oteh (coverest) in Who coverest Thyself with light (Tehillim 104:2). He shall cover his upper lip so that he does not harm anyone with the breath of his mouth.
And…unclean. The word unclean is repeated. When the leper passes on a road in an inhabited area he shall continually announce that he is unclean so that people will be on guard and not touch him.
All the days wherein the plague is in him he shall be unclean. For he is truly unclean.
The word badad (alone) is explained in the Book of Eichah.

Or in the warp, or in the woof. The meaning of sheti (warp) and erev (woof) is known. It is possible that the word sheti is related to the word shet (buttocks) in ve-chasufe shet (buttocks uncovered) (Is. 20:4) wherein the word shet means the foundation, as the clause When the foundations (ha-shatot) are destroyed (Tehillim 11:3) proves.
The word erev (woof) refers to that which is mixed with the warp.
Or in the skin. As it is.
Or in any thing made of skin. Such as a coverlet (Melachim II 8:15) or a bottle (Jud. 4:19).

Greenish. The word yerakrak (greenish) is related to the word yerek (green), for the color of the affliction is like it. The word is doubled to indicate that it is less than full green. The same applies to shecharchoret (swarthy) (Cant. 1:6). Others say that the reverse is true.

Malignant. The word mameret (malignant) is similar to the word mammir (pricking) in a pricking brier (sillon mamir) (Yechezkel 28:24). Now, since the word sillon (brier) means a thorn, the word mamir means painful. The second mem in mameret is a root letter and the word mameret is not related to the word me’erah (curse). It is possible that the reason Scripture does not mention silk and cotton is that the Torah speaks of what is contemporarily present. Compare, If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee (Shemot 23:5). The same law applies to a horse and a mule. On the other hand, it is possible that the affliction only strikes wool and flax.
After that the plague is washed. The word hukkabbes (is washed) is an infinitive whose subject is not identified. It is in the hofal.

A fret. The word pechetet (fret) has no brother in Scripture. It is known in Rabbinic literature. Pechetet refers to a defect which appears in the karachat (bareness…within) or the gabachat (bareness…without) of the garments. The Gaon says that karachat refers to the underside of the garment, for gabachat refers to the face of the garment. If this is the case, then the word kere’ach (bald) (v. 40) refers to the back of the head. He explained well.

And if it appear still. The word tera’eh (it appear) refers to the pechetet (the fret). Similarly porachat hi (it is breaking out). After stating thou shalt burn [it], Scripture goes on to say that the place of the affliction alone shall be burned.
Then it shall be washed the second time. There is divine command to wash it twice.
If the plague be departed from them. Ve-sar me-hem ha-naga means if the plague be departed from them. I have previously shown you many such instances.
Ve-khubbas (it shall be washed) is a pu’al.

This is the law of the plague of leprosy in a garment of wool. Our verse has four words in the construct. Elsewhere in Scripture we find five words in the construct. Compare, Gibore chayil melechet avodat bet haElokim (very able men for the work of the service of the house of Hashem) (Divrei Hayamim I 9:13). They all depend (semukhim) on Hashem, who supports (somekh) all who fall.

[And Hashem spoke.] Scripture states and Hashem spoke because it begins the laws of the one who is cleansed. Rabbi Yonah the Spaniard, the grammarian, says that and, behold, if the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper (v. 3) is inverted. It should have read “and, behold, if the leper be healed from the plague of leprosy.”

[He shall be brought.] He shall be brought is to be interpreted like its counterparts, for it is possible that after the plague of leprosy is removed the afflicted person will not want to bring what he is obligated to.

And the priest shall go forth out of the camp. Even though the kohen declared him clean he shall not enter the camp or the city until he brings his cleanliness offerings and completes all that he has been commanded to do.
And the priest shall go forth. The reference is not to the kohen gadol. The meaning of or unto one of his sons the priests (Vayikra 13:2) has now been clarified.

To take for him that is to be cleansed. The kohen shall take of his own. Some say that the leper shall give them. The tav of the hitpa’el form is swallowed by the dagesh in the tet of mittaher (cleansed). The word mittaher follows the form of mithallel (boasteth himself) in he that boasteth himself (Mishlei 25:14).
Two…birds. The term tzippor applies to all birds. Note, he shall take any bird that he finds.
Living. Not dead.
Clean. He shall not take from the unclean.

And cedar-wood…and hyssop. These are the biggest and smallest among the plants. This is proven by Scripture’s description of Shlomo’s wisdom. There is no reason to search for the meaning of the word ezov (hyssop), for it is known by tradition. Note, the leper and the plagued house and uncleanness caused by a corpse are similar. They are also similar to the Mitzri Passover.
And the priest shall command to kill. The priest shall command another kohen or a Yisraeli. Some say he shall command the leper. However, the latter is farfetched.
In an earthen vessel. The word el (in) is to be rendered as over. Similarly el (for) in For this child I prayed (Shmuel I 1:27).
Over running water. Taken from a bubbling fountain.
And shall dip them. The cedar-wood, the scarlet, and the hyssop.
Over…water. With which the blood was mixed.
And he shall sprinkle. From the blood mixed with water after immersing the living bird and the other items mentioned.

Into the open field. An uninhabited place so that the leprosy does not infect anyone. The sprinkling was done with all three. On the other hand, it might only have been done with the hyssop as in the case of one who has been made unclean by a corpse.
And…shall wash his clothes and shave off all his hair. A general statement.

And bathe himself in water, and he shall be clean. In the evening, as is the law. After stating this, Scripture backtracks and explains that this occurs after seven days. The same law applied to the seven days of Miriam. Scripture details that he shall shave all his hair on the seventh day. Scripture then goes on to explain that the meaning of all his hair is, the hair on his head, his beard, and his eyebrows. The word gabbot (eyebrows) is close in meaning to the word gav (high place).
Even all his hair. The hair of the feet. Some say the hair of his arms, thighs, and chest.

Two he-lambs…and one ewe-lamb. The leper shall bring a he-lamb for a burnt offering as is the law regarding all who have evil thoughts, because the plague of leprosy is a punishment for deeds of the tongue. Another he-lamb is brought as a guilt offering as is the law with all guilt offerings. A ewe-lamb is offered for a sin offering as is the law with all sin offerings. Also three tenth parts of an ephah as is the law, for a tenth part of an ephah is brought with a lamb.

And one log. A measure. The term log has no brother. [11. AND THOSE THINGS.] This refers to the he-lambs and the ewe-lamb. Also, this guilt offering and also the sin offering, with the exception of the parts offered on the altar, belong to the kohen.

Upon the tip. The meaning of tenuch (tip) is understood from its context. Now, the one who is cleansed from leprosy, which is an affliction in the body, is similar to the kohen who is installed, for sin is like a leprosy in the soul. The thumb is the place of connection. It is the main component of all acts. The right thumb was selected because of the power of the right side. The tip of the ear is a reminder to listen to what God has commanded.

Into the palm of his own left hand. The palm in kaf ha-kohen (the palm of his own) refers to the palm of the kohen who cleanses. Scripture reads thus because such style is considered elegant in the Hebrew language. The verse that follows is proof of this.
Before Hashem. Towards the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Upon the blood of the guilt-offering. Which is upon the tip, the thumb, and the great toe.
And the priest shall offer the sin-offering. The ewe-lamb as is the law with all sin offerings.

And the priest shall offer the burnt-offering. The he-lamb and its meal offering, which consists of a tenth of an ephah. Some say that the kohen shall offer the entire meal offering with the burnt offering. He shall offer the guilt offering first because it is more severe.
And he shall be clean. Then he shall be clean like all who are clean.

And if he be poor. The term dal (poor) is found with regard to the body. Compare, poor (dal) and very ill-favored (Bereshit 41:19); Happy is he that considereth the poor (dal) (Tehillim 41:2); son of the king, art thou thus becoming leaner (dal) (Shmuel II 13:4). The term dal is also found with regard to one who has no money.
And Hashem spoke unto Moshe and unto Aharon. Scripture begins explaining the laws dealing with leprosy in a house.

[When ye are come into the land of Kenaan.] Scripture reads thus because this law applies only in the Land of Yisrael because of the great status of the land; for the temple was among them, and the Glory was in the midst of the temple.
And I put. The event is contingent on Hashem’s putting.
Then he that owneth the house shall come. There is a divine command that he come to the kohen.
That they empty the house. The master of the house and all men of his household. Scripture employs the plural for it is to be emptied quickly.
Before the priest go in. For the kohen will close up the house because of its uncertain status. The house shall be emptied before its status is declared to be in doubt.

Hollow streaks. The word sheka’arurot (hollow streaks) has no sister. We do not know if it is a quadrilateral with the last letter doubled or if it is a pentaliteral. The meaning of sheka’arurot is to be ascertained from its context. Some say that it refers to marks or streaks. Others say that it is a compound word. It is akin to va-tishka (sank down) in and the fire sank down (Bamidbar 11:2) and to rorot, which is related to the word rar (run) in run with his issue (Vayikra 15:3). However, this is far-fetched.
And the appearance thereof. The appearance of each one of them be lower [than the wall].
That they take out the stones. Ve-chilletzu means that they take out. Compare, challetzeni (deliver me) in Deliver me, O Hashem, from the evil man (Tehillim 140:2).
Into an unclean place. So that no one remove the stones from there. So that it be recognized that they are unclean.

And he shall cause the house to be scraped. The word yaktzi’a (he shall cause…to be scraped) is related to the word maktzu’ot (planes) (Is. 44:13) and the word ketzi’ot (cassia) in Myrrh, and aloes, and cassia (Tehillim 45:9). The meaning of ketz’ot (cassia) is cuttings. Some say the corner shall be peeled. However, this is incorrect, for the plague had already spread in the house. Actually, he must scrape the whole house.
The meaning of mi-bayit means within.
The word hiktzu (they scrape off) is related to the word katzeh (extremity), for they only removed the upper extremity.

And shall plaster the house. The word tach (plaster) is the reverse of yaktzi’a (he shall cause…to be scraped) (v. 41). It is related to tachim (daub) in they daub it with whited plaster (Yechezkel 13:10).

After the house hath been scraped. After the stones have first been taken out and the house has been scraped. Scripture employs the plural forms ve-lakechu (and they shall take) and ve-hevi’u (and put them) to indicate haste.
And he shall take other mortar. The owner of the house who wants to dwell in the house.
If the plague returns (v. 43), then the kohen shall come (v. 44).

And he shall break down the house. By command. Similarly and he shall carry them forth. It is most likely that the house was shut up for seven days. However, Scripture employed an abridged style. He that goeth into the house all the while that it is shut up (v. 46) which applies to the first and second times is proof of this.
Shall be unclean until the even. After he bathes his body as the law requires.

And he that lieth. This is very severe uncleanliness. He that lies in the house must therefore wash his garments and bathe and be unclean until evening. Scripture does not mention that he be unclean until evening, for whoever lies and eats in the house, first comes into the house.
And he shall take. This is to be interpreted as its counterpart.
When it is unclean. The day when the man or the garment or the house will be unclean or clean.

And Hashem spoke unto Moshe and to Aharon. For the kohanim distinguish between a woman who has an issue (zavah) and one who menstruates (niddah). Compare the Rabbinic interpretation on between blood and blood (Devarim 17:8). Scripture now begins to deal with those who become unclean from a hidden source, for until now it dealt with leprosy which is a visible plague.
An issue. The word zav (issue) is similar to the word zavat (flowing) in flowing with milk (Shemot 44:13). Zav refers to dripping drops.
Out of his flesh. A euphemism for the male’s private part.
His issue. Zovo (his issue) is a noun.
And this shall be his uncleanliness. This means the issue takes two forms.
His flesh run with his issue. The word rar (run) is related to the word riro (his spittle) in, and let his spittle fall down upon his beard (Shmuel I 21:14).

Or be stopped. The word hechtim means stopped. It is related to the word chatum (sealed) in that is sealed (Is. 29:11). It means that the issue pools and congeals so that semen is not ejaculated when the afflicted sleeps with a women.
The same law applies to what the one who has an issue lies or sits on. Similarly, there is one law regarding the one who touches what the afflicted lies on or sits on.
Ands he that toucheth the flesh of him that hath the issue. Any part without exception.

Spit. The meaning of yarok (spit) is known. It comes from a double root. The fact that the kof of rukki (my spittle) (Iyov 7:19) has a dagesh is proof of this. Note, the spit of the one who suffers an issue is harmful, for the issue is one of the infectious diseases. It is not the practice of men to spit in the face of other people. What happened occurred unintentionally. The one suffering from an issue expectorated his spittle and it fell on a clean person.
And what saddle. Which, as the transmitters of tradition explained, becomes unclean.
Any thing that is under him. Under the saddle shall become lightly unclean. However, the uncleanliness of those who carry them is more strict.

Without having rinsed his hands in water. It would have appeared to us that any food or anything similar, that the one having an issue touched by hand, and the hands were washed, is not unclean, for the afflicted did not touch the place of the issue. However, since we saw that our fathers explained that the hands are like the body we accept their words. According to the plain meaning of our verse if the one experiencing an issue touches someone with hands that have been washed the one touched is unclean but his garments are not unclean. However, if the one suffering the issue did not wash his hands then the garments are unclean. This law is similar to the one regarding he who touches anything which is under the saddle.
For his cleansing. From the day of his cleansing.
The sacrifice consists of a burnt-offering and a sin-offering, for the issue is a punishment for sin.
Go out. Involuntarily.
Flow of seed. Shikhvat (flow) is similar to shikhvat (layer) in the layer of dew (Shemot 16:14). It is related to the word yashkiv (pour out) in who can pour out (Iyov 38:37).
It would appear to us that the garment or the skin requires washing if it has wet semen or dry semen on it. However, the truth lies with the words of tradition.
Scripture concludes the laws of the male. It then begins with the female.

In her flesh. In the women’s private part. Those who explain then he shall bathe all his flesh (v. 16) which is written concerning one who ejaculates as referring to the penis err. The word all is proof.

The meaning of And if he be on the bed (v. 23) refers back to the object that she sits upon (v. 22). Now the object is on the bed or the object is on another object. The uncleanliness is therefore light. Scripture does not mention a saddle with regards to a women for Scripture speaks of what is prevalent. The law is the same.

And if any man lie with her. Without any sinful intent. On the contrary, he erred in sleeping with her. Behold her menstrual flow came while he was with her. This is the meaning of be upon him, for the one who sleeps with a menstruating women incurs the penalty of karet. The same law applies to a women who has an issue, even though it is not stated.
And every bed whereon he lieth shall be unclean. For he is unclean for seven days. He also defiles others. The latter is so even though it is not stated.
Many days not in the time of her impurity. Every women has fixed periods. Or, she had an issue added to her menstruation.
And bring them. Ve-hevi’ah (and bring them) is ultimately accented. It is an irregular word.

Thus shall ye separate. Some say that ve-hizzartem (thus shall ye separate) is missing a heh and is to be interpreted ve-hizzhartem (and you shall warn). This cannot be so, for the heh is not vowel letter. It is only silent at the end of a word. On the contrary, ve-hizzartem is related to the word ve-yinnazeru (that they separate) in that they separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Yisrael (Vayikra 22:2). The meaning of that ve-hizzartem is, and you shall distance. The word nazir (nazirite) is derived from the same root. A nazir is one who has distanced himself from the lusts of the world. Ve-hizzartem is vocalized like the word ve-hippaltem (and you shall divide) in, and you shall divide the land (Yechezkel 45:1), for the nun is swallowed in the dagesh.
In their uncleanliness. Be-tumatam (in their uncleanliness) is to be rendered because of their uncleanliness. Its meaning is, when they defile My tabernacle.
So that he is unclean thereby. There is a Divine command for him to be in a state of ritual impurity. I will explain this later.
Whether it be a man explains the law of him that hath an issue (v. 32).
With her that is unclean refers to a women who has an issue or menstruates.

After the death. After Hashem warned Yisrael not to incur the death penalty He also told Moshe to caution Aharon not to die as his sons died. This section is proof that the sons of Aharon brought the incense within the veil.

[When they drew near.] The word be-korvatam (when they drew near) is an infinitive. Compare, le-korvah (to come unto) in to come unto the work (Shemot 36:2). The heh in le-korvah has been turned into a tav in be-korvatam as is the practice with the feminine heh. Rabbi Yehoshua, who says that be-korvatam is a noun following the paradigm of chokhmatam (their wisdom) (Yirmiyahu 49:7), errs.
Into the holy place. In contrast to the tent of meeting.

For I appear in the cloud. It means Aharon shall only enter with incense. He shall produce smoke so that Hashem’s glory will not be seen, and as a result he dies. Note, the meaning of ki be-anan era’eh (for I appear in the cloud upon the ark-cover) is, I will not appear to him except through the agency of a cloud. There are those who say that the meaning of ki be-anan era’eh al ha-kapporet (for I appear in the cloud) is, because I dwell in a cloud upon the ark-covering. For I appear in the cloud is similar in meaning to Hashem hath said that He would dwell in the thick darkness (Melachim I 8:12).

With a young bullock. Its meaning is not that Aharon should bring the bullock into the holy place but rather that he first bring a bullock of his own for a sin offering to atone for himself and the kohanim. Others say also for the Leviyim, for they found, And thou shalt write Aharon’s name upon the rod of Levi (Bamidbar 17:18). However, this is farfetched. On the contrary, the Leviyim are considered among Bnei Yisrael.

The holy linen tunic. Scripture does not mention the ephod, the breastplate, and the robe of the ephod, for it earlier mentioned, and the sound thereof shall be heard when he goeth in unto the holy place (Shemot 28:35). The men of the second temple who served without the Urim and the Tumim learned from this verse [that their practice was proper]. There were also prophets there.
And Aharon shall present the bullock of the sin-offering, which is for himself. To the opening of the tent of meeting as is the law.

[And make atonement for himself.] This means that with it he will make atonement for himself and for his house after he slaughters it. There are those who say that presenting the bullock is the atonement.

Lots. We know what they are from the words of our sages. The Gaon says that Azazel is the name of a mountain. It is so called because of its might. Hashem’s name is mentioned in Azazel as it is in ke-harere el (the mighty mountains) (Tehillim 36:7) and in yakti’el (Yokte'el) (Melachim II 14:7). The Gaon, the Levi, caught him in error. He pointed out that the alef of Azazel is placed between one zayin and the other zayin. There are those who say that Azazel is the name of a mountain close to Mount Sinai. Hashem commanded that the goat be led and brought up there until it slipped down the mountain. Later on in the time of the temple, they led it to a different mountain. “And Aharon did” (v. 34) is proof of this. The same, in my opinion, as I will explain in its place, is true of the festival of Shavu’ot. There are those who say that the service during the second temple was unlike that of the first, for the kohen lacked the garments and there was no ark-cover. This commentator says that the goat was sent into the wilderness, for Scripture states, and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness (v. 22). The latter is similar in meaning to the bird of the one who is cleansed from leprosy which is sent into the open field, an uninhabited place. A land which is cut off (v. 22) is proof of this. We answered him that they sent the goat into the wilderness as it is written. However, the goat was pursued until it fled and climbed up a rock. The rabbis therefore said, “and he pushes it down.” Rabbi Shmuel says that even though it is written that the goat offered as a sin offering is to be offered to Hashem, the goat that was sent was also offered to Hashem. There is no need for this interpretation, for the goat sent into the wilderness did not serve as an offering since it was not slaughtered. If you are able to understand the secret that follows Azazel then you will know its secret and the secret of its name, for it has comrades in Scripture. I will reveal a bit of its secret to you in a hint. When you are thirty-three, you will understand it.
And offer him for a sin-offering. He shall slaughter it.

Shall be set alive. The word yo’omad (shall be set) is a hofal. The yod should have been vocalized with a shuruk. However, it was enlarged because of the guttural. The word yochoram (should be forfeited) in all his substance should be forfeited (Ez. 10:8) is similar.
To make atonement over him. For the atonement shall be upon it. It means to send him away.

And Aharon shall present. Scripture goes on to explain that after Aharon has presented the bullock and the two goats to the tent of meeting, he shall begin to slaughter his bullock. Scripture does this because it dwelt at length on the goats.
A censer. The meaning of machtah (censer) is known.
His hands full. Both hands.
Sweet incense. Mentioned earlier.

It would have appeared to us that upon the ark-cover (v. 14); and before the arkcover (Ibid.) are to be taken literally. However, the transmitters of tradition said that upon the ark-cover means between the staves. The meaning of and before the ark-cover is known from their words. What they said is true.

Then shall he kill the goat of the sin-offering. He shall now, when he goes out, slaughter it. There are those who say that he should slaughter the goat before he slaughters the bullock. The latter is untrue.
And he shall make atonement for the holy place. The reference is to the Holy of Holies.
And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting. He shall sprinkle seven times before the ark-cover (kaporet) and on the horns of the altar of incense.
The meaning of And he shall make atonement for the holy place is that the blood serves as a ransom so that the holy place does not destroy because of the uncleanliness of the unclean.
And there shall be no man. From among the kohanim.
To make atonement in the holy place. Inside.
And have made atonement for himself, and for his household. With his sin offering bullock.
And for all the assembly of Yisrael. With their sin offering goat.
And he shall go out unto the altar. The reference is to the burnt offering altar.

And he shall put them. After the sins are removed from Yisrael they are, as it were, placed on the head of the goat. The sins will go to a place were they will never again be remembered. Scripture speaks in a way that all will understand.

Appointed. Itti (appointed) means prepared for his time. Or itti refers to an individual whose custom it was to always lead the goat on the Day of Atonement. The yod relates to the word et (time). Itti is similar to penimi (internal). The interpretation of those who explain itti to mean wise does not appear correct to me. Our sages, of blessed memory, said that the “bearer” was a kohen. Their words are true.
In a holy place. In the courtyard of the tent of meeting. They used to spread a sheet for the kohen.

His other vestments. With which he serves every day. There are those who say that the reference is to the garments mentioned. The fact that Scripture does not say and put on other garments (Vayikra 6:4) is proof of this.
His burnt-offering. The reference is to the ram and the ram of the people, the bullock of the people, and the seven lambs, for it is so written in Scripture.

And the fat of the sin-offering. The fat of the bullock sin offering and the fat of the goat sin offering and also the fat of the he-goat sin offering, which is a sin offering belonging to the kohen as is the law, and is not burned. The last named sacrifice is found in the Torah portion Pinechas.
And bathe his flesh in water. This is sufficient for him, for he does not become unclean until evening.
Shall be carried forth without the camp. By command.

And they shall burn. The kohanim shall burn them. All those who do the burning shall bathe in water and immediately come into the camp. The fact that Scripture immediately states, and afterward he may come into the camp, is proof of this, for what reason is there to states this.
And it shall be a statute for ever unto you. This service.

In the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls. Since Scripture writes, And let your soul delight itself in fatness (Is. 55:2), we know that affliction is the reverse of delight and that affliction of the soul refers to fasting. Furthermore, Scripture states, And satisfy the afflicted soul (Is. 58:10), the meaning of which is like And if thou draw out thy soul to the hungry (Ibid.), for it is the style of the prophets to repeat themselves. Now since we have tradition there is no reason to go on searching. I afflicted my soul with fasting (Tehillim 35:13) is no proof because the word fast is mentioned. The general rule is, whenever we find in Scripture the word affliction connected to soul, the reference is to a fast.
The home-born, or the stranger that sojourneth among you. We are not permitted to let him do any work, but we do not force him to fast.

Shall atonement be made for you. By the kohen. The commentators therefore say regarding the goat which is sent into the wilderness, concerning which it is written, shall be set alive…to make atonement over him (v. 10), that the atonement becomes effective by the placing of the goat before the Lord.

From all your sins. This is to be understood in accordance with my earlier explanation that the noun chattat (sin) is a general term. It is therefore found with reference to both accidental and deliberate sin.

It is a Sabbath of solemn rest. Some say that shabbat shabbaton (a sabbath of solemn rest) means rest for the soul and rest for the body. Others say that shabbat shabbaton means a rest above which there is no other rest. Both words are nouns. At times the other word comes first. They have one meaning, This interpretation is not farfetched.
It is a statute for ever. To fast.
And the priest…shall make atonement. Scripture now goes on to explain what the kohen shall make atonement for.
Who shall be anointed. By the anointer with the anointing oil after he has been consecrated.
And he shall put on. He is the one who shall put on these holy garments, for another person may not wear them.
The most holy place. Which is located on the inner side of the veil.

And shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly. The Leviyim are included among the latter, for the Leviyim are not called kohanim. On the contrary, every kohen is a Levi but every Levi is not a kohen.
And this shall be…unto you. Scripture already stated this. It is repeated to add once in the year.
And he did. And Aharon did.
Speak unto Aharon, and unto his sons. For they are the ones who slaughter for Yisrael.

If the Torah had read, in the camp (v. 3), then it would have been permissible to slaughter it outside the camp. Also, this commandment is dependent upon the Holy Temple. However, this law applies only to any place that is close to Yerushalayim. We know how close from the words of tradition, for if the place is far, one is permitted to slaughter flesh. The latter is so, for Scripture states it. Many say that it is forbidden to eat flesh in the exile. They explain neither came flesh nor wine in my mouth (Daniel 10:3) as referring to the flesh of fish. They did not speak correctly. I do not want to dwell on this and answer them.
To the end that the children of Yisrael may bring. This is the reason for this commandment. And they shall no more sacrifice their sacrifices unto the satyrs (v. 7) explains in the open field.

Unto the satyrs. Se’irim (satyrs) are the demons. They are so called because the body of one who sees them “storms.” However, it appears that they are so called because the insane see them in the form of goats (se’irim). The word “more” teaches that Bnei Yisrael did so in Mitzrayim.

After whom they go astray. For whoever seeks after them and believes in them strays from under his Elokim, for he thinks that there is someone aside from Hashem the glorious and awe inspiring who does good or bad. This section does not mention the stranger, for the commandment regarding sacrifices and burnt offerings falls on Yisrael. Scripture mentions the stranger in order to teach that Yisrael shall not permit a stranger to sacrifice to idols in the Land of Yisrael. The law regarding all manner of blood (v. 10) is similar. The eating of blood is prohibited because it is the very life, for the flesh lives by the blood. The truth of the matter is that the life by which a person lives is in the blood which is in the heart.

That maketh atonement by reason of the life. The blood makes atonement by the life which is in it. The reason for the latter is life for life. There are others who explain ba-nefesh yekhapper (that maketh atonement by reason of the life) as, to make atonement for your souls. However, the latter makes no sense, for what reason is there for Scripture to say this after stating to make atonement for your souls?
That taketh in hunting any beast or fowl that may be eaten. Such as a deer or a gazelle.

Or fowl that may be eaten. We also learn from this verse that we should not allow the stranger to eat in our land the flesh of a pig or a horse, or any bird of prey which is unclean. It is possible that Hashem commanded that all blood which is not offered on the altar be covered so that the one who sees the blood of the deer, stag, or fowl not think that it comes from a sacrifice that was offered to an idol, for Hashem had commanded that no blood be eaten and that no blood from Hashem’s altar be spilled outside of the altar. I will explain the secret of this verse in the Torah portion opening with the words Behold, I set (Devarim 11:26).

The blood thereof is all one with the life thereof. The blood is coupled with the life thereof, for it is known that the threads that go out from the left side of the heart are divided, half for blood and half for the breath, like the olive oil and the light thereof.
Therefore I said unto the children of Yisrael. The meaning of va-omar (therefore I said) is, and I have previously said. The reference is to the section now mentioned.

Since Scripture mentions the beast (chayyah) which is not offered as a sacrifice, and similarly the fowl, it goes on to speak of every soul that eateth that which dieth of itself (v. 15), which is also not offered as a sacrifice. Scripture also mentions the latter because of its reference to an animal which is taken in hunting. If one does so deliberately he violates a negative precept and is flogged. If he does so accidentally, he brings a sin offering. If one should argue, does not Scripture state, thou mayest give it unto the stranger that is within thy gates, that he may eat it (Devarim 14:21)? The answer is that this speaks of a stranger who dwells in the Land of Yisrael. Scripture similarly reads, or the stranger that sojourneth among you (Vayikra 16:29). We shall not allow him to eat anything that dies of itself. However, we may give it to the stranger that comes into our gates and he will eat it outside.

Then he shall bear his iniquity. Permanently. He will be forgiven for his sin by the punishment which Hashem shall bring upon him. This section follows because Scripture mentioned the topic of the satyrs which Yisrael sacrificed to in Mitzrayim. The prohibited sexual practices deal with those of the land of Kenaan, for Scripture so states at the end.
[I am Hashem your Elokim.] The meaning of this verse is, on this condition I will be your Elokim.
Neither shall ye walk in their statutes. A person should not habituate himself to walk in this way to the point where it becomes a statute for him.

However, after the doings of the land of Mitzrayim refers to their ordinances. Mine ordinances (mishpatai) shall ye do (v. 4) is proof of this. The latter refers to the ordinances recorded in the Book of the Covenant, which is set forth in the Torah portion that opens with Now these are the ordinances (mishpatim) (Shemot 21:1).
I am Hashem your Elokim. I will then be your Elokim.

The reason Scripture states, Ye shall therefore keep My statutes, and Mine ordinances (v. 5) is to make it clear that they are a source of life in both worlds to those who observe them. Elokim will give eternal life to the person who understands their secret. He will never die. Scripture, as I have explained, therefore reads, I am Hashem your Elokim.

None of you. Ish ish (none of you) means each and every man. Since Scripture does not mention the house of Yisrael, we learn that we are not permitted to allow the stranger to practice in our country any of the abominations mentioned, so that he does not defile the land.

Any that is near of kin to him. She’er (near) is a general term for all those with whom one is prohibited to engage in sexual relations. Scripture then goes into detail. Rabbi Aharon Ha-Kohen says that the reference is to the emission of semen in vain.
None of you shall approach. Approach is a euphemism for lying with. Similarly And I approached the prophetess (Is. 8:3). Our verse is close to come not near a woman (Shemot 19:15).
Nakedness. Ervah (nakedness) refers to something unseemly which is exposed and has to be covered.

The meaning of I am Hashem is that Hashem loves the one who separates himself to serve Hashem and to obey his word. What happened at Mount Sinai is proof. The first man is proof. This is the secret of man. Since the inclination of the heart of man is like that of beasts, it was not possible to prohibit all women. Note, Scripture prohibited all women that are found around a person at all times. I will reveal to you a hidden and sealed secret in the Torah portion When thou goest forth in camp against thine enemies (Devarim 23:10). Observe, whoever defiles himself is distanced from Hashem, from receiving Hashem. Scripture therefore mentions, I am Hashem.

The nakedness of thy father. Scripture begins with the father, who precedes the son. Scripture states that anyone who is closely related to his father or mother is prohibited. Note, the nakedness of the mother is the one that is mentioned first. The nakedness of the father’s wife, who is not the mother, follows. Then comes the sister, who is the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.
Born at home. Who was born in accordance with the laws of the house of Yisrael following the first and second stage of marriage.

Born abroad. Unconventionally. Some say that born at home is similar to were born upon Yosef’s knees (Bereshit 50:23). It means she grew up with you in the same house. It is possible that born abroad means she is in a different place and a different city and grew up away from you, outside of your father’s house. Scripture next mentions thy son’s daughter (v. 10).

The nakedness of thy father’s wife’s daughter. There are those who say that this refers to a sister from a father and mother. We know that the one who sleeps with a sister from a father and mother violates two negative laws. There are those who say that our verse was written for emphasis. The Sadducees say that thy father’s wife’s daughter does not refer to the daughter of one’s mother. They explain that begotten of thy father means whom your father raised. Our verse deals with an instance in which the father took a woman who had a small daughter. They say the same thing regarding Tamar. Their proof is, for he will not withhold me from thee (Shmuel II 13:13). She thus was not begotten by David. Now since the transmitters of tradition said that the daughter of your father’s wife is permitted, we have no need to answer those who invent things in their hearts. It is possible that “the daughter of thy father’s wife” refers to a daughter resulting from a rape.
The word she’er (kin) and basar (kin) are close in meaning.

She is thine aunt. She is considered as your aunt. Similarly “Behold Chanamel, my uncle.” Now what will those who rely on the Torah alone for the commandments do? For Scripture does not prohibit the wife of the brother of one’s mother, and not the mother of one’s father, or the mother of one’s mother. We therefore need tradition. It is possible that the reason that Scripture did not mention that the wife of one’s mother’s brother is prohibited is that we learn this from the prohibition of the wife of the father’s brother. The prohibition of the wife of one’s brother is mentioned in the Torah (Vayikra 19:3) portion Ye shall be holy. Also, the reason that those whom I mentioned are not listed in Scripture is that the Torah speaks of that which is prevalent.
Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy brother’s wife. This is explained in the Torah portion If brethren dwell together (Devarim 25:5).

To the one who asks why didn’t Scripture mention a daughter, [I reply] that the daughter is stated in Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter (Vayikra 18:17), whether or not it is his daughter, for once he has slept with the mother the daughter is prohibited.
They are near kinswomen. She’er (kin) and sha’arah (kinswomen) are two nouns. If the alef of sha’arah were not a guttural, it would be quiescent like the lamed of salmah (raiment) (Shemot 22:8).

To be a rival. Li-tzeror (to be a rival) is related to the word tzaratah (her rival) in And her rival vexed her (Shmuel I 1:6). Note, Scripture does not mention in the Torah portion Ye shall be holy (Vayikra 19:2) the punishment for sleeping with two sisters, and it does not mention the punishment for sleeping with the daughter of one’s son and with the daughter of one’s daughter. The one who says that Rachel and Leah were not sisters errs. His proof is, for all these abominations… (Vayikra 18:27). However, this is not a rigorous proof. There are those who answer the one who asks, how could Hashem punish for something He did not warn against, by saying the sons of Noach were warned about these sexual offenses. Others say that even though Scripture makes a general statement, for all these abominations…, the reference is not to all these abominations but to most of them. You will learn my opinion in the Torah portion And Moshe went (Devarim 31:1).
One who sleeps with a menstruating woman is considered to have slept with a woman whose nakedness one is prohibited from uncovering.

With thy neighbor’s wife. This excludes the captive woman. There are those who say that she was previously prohibited. Those whose sexual craving overcame the intelligence of their heart erred in explaining the meaning of le-zara (carnally). We know that sexual intercourse is divided into three groups. One, to be fruitful and multiply and not to satisfy lust. Two, to relieve the fullness of the body. Three, for the purpose of lust, which is similar to the lust of an animal. Now since Scripture says le-zara (carnally), the meaning of which is even for seed, a married woman is prohibited by a very severe prohibition. And thou shalt not give any of thy seed to set them apart to Molech (v. 21) is proof. Scripture adds to defile thyself with her to let us know that the one who touches her will not be cleansed; he will be defiled forever. This verse does not at all prohibit a non-Jewish woman. There is no argument from the captive woman, for she converts to Judaism.

To Molech. Molech is the name of an image. The rabbis interpreted Molech as a general term for all whom a person accepts as a king over him. It is possible that Molech is the abomination of Bnei Amon.

The word le-ha’avir (to set apart) is to burn, for that was the way Molech was worshipped. Some say that they used to pass their sons over the fire. Some lived and some died. In view of the fact that the verse does not mention fire, some explained le-ha’avir lamolekh (to set apart to Molech) as meaning to cause to pass over from the Torah of Elokim to another religion. You will defile Hashem who is known as your Elokim when you give from the holy seed to Molech. The Gaon says that fornication has eight levels. The most severe is intercourse with a beast of another species; afterwards comes the male, the entire gender of which is prohibited; afterwards comes the nakedness of the father’s wife and her companions, which are prohibited at all times. I will not dwell on this, for what purpose is there to these words since Scripture says, concerning all of them, even the souls that do them shall be cut off (v. 29).

With mankind. Since we find, Behold, I lay yester-night with my father (Bereshit 19:34), we see that the prohibition applies to the one who lay and the one who is lain with. Rabbi Hannanel, of blessed memory, says that there are those in whose body a female genitalia is newly formed. However, this is impossible according to the laws of nature. There are those who say that the reference is to an androgynous person. All this pain was caused by the fact that Scripture employs the plural mishkeve ishah (as with womankind). There is an individual opinion that mishkeve ishah refers to two types of intercourse. I believe that the precept is to be taken literally. The men of sound wisdom also applied the death penalty to those who performed this act. Scripture employed respectable language in saying [thou shalt not lie]. Compare, thou shalt not approach (v. 14). Now, since the male was created to make and the female to be made, Scripture notes that one should not reverse the words of Hashem. There is a type of laying whose aim is to emit semen. Hence Scripture employs the term mishkeve which is a plural. It is unfit to dwell at length on this.
Scripture states it is abomination, for it is an abomination to a holy soul even by the laws of nature.

I have already explained the word shekhovtekha (lie carnally). It is possible that the word shekhovtekha is derived from shekhivah (lying), for the emission of semen comes along with lying. As Scripture states to defile thyself with her (v. 20) with regard to a married woman, it similarly says so with regard to a beast.
And…any beast. A female beast.
Before a beast. A male beast.
To lie down thereto. Le-rivah reverts to the beast, for the woman is the one who is penetrated. The word rivah (lie down) is related to the word arba’ah (four).

It is perversion. The grammarians say that the word tevel (perversion) comes from a double root. Compare, temes (melteth) in which melteth and passeth away (Tehillim 58:9). The tav of tevel is superfluous. They say that tevel means destruction. There are those who say that the word mabbul (flood) is related to it. However, the word mabbul is most likely related to the word balal (confound) in Hashem did there confound the language of all the earth (Bereshit 11:9). This is the general rule: Scripture prohibits all kinds of women with which it is possible for a person to be alone; a married woman, a non-Jewish woman, and those with whom intercourse cannot result in children, for a kind cannot reproduce except with its own kind and with those like its kind.

Defile not ye yourselves. The tet of tittamme’u (defile ye yourselves) has a dagesh to compensate for the swallowed tav of the hitpa’el. The dagesh does not compensate for the nun of the nifal. The dagesh in the mem of tittamme’u, which is there according to the rules of grammar, is proof of this. Observe, Scripture notes that each one of these acts defiles the soul.
Which I cast out from before you. It means, from the Holy Land, dead or expelled.
And the land vomited out her inhabitants. Whatever a person regurgitates is despised in his eyes, and he will not take it back.
Ye therefore shall keep my statutes. The very ones that I enumerated shall be prohibited to you.

And mine ordinances. You shall execute the judgment which I will command, upon the one who violates any of these. The reason that and shall not do any of these abominations is written a second time is to include the stranger, for this precept applies equally to the native and to the stranger who dwells in the Land of Yisrael. If you have any intelligence you can understand why in past days Yaakov took two sisters in Charan and later Amram took his aunt in Mitzrayim, and they were not defiled through them.

The meaning of for all these abominations (Vayikra 18:27) is, you and your children shall know this so that you shall keep these precepts, and the land will be pure and the land will not regurgitate you.
These. Ha-el (these) and ha-elleh (these) (v. 29) have one meaning. Compare, ha-hem (those) and ha-hemah (those). However, this is not the opinion of the Gaon.

As it vomited out. Ka’ah (vomited out) is a verb in the perfect. It is related to the word keyo (spew) in Drink ye, and be drunken, and spew (Yirmiyahu 25:27), for the letters alef, heh, vav, yod interchange. The word eretz is found in the masculine. Compare, netam aretz (the land burnt up) (Is. 9:18), and ve-lo nasa otam ha-aretz (and the land was not able to bear them) (Bereshit 13:6). On the other hand, the word hiy (it) might be missing. Our verse should be interpreted as if it read, ka’asher hiy ka’ah (as it vomited out). In this case, ka’ah is similar to ba’ah (cometh) in cometh with the sheep (Bereshit 29:6).
Even the souls that do them shall be cut off. If they do so in public you shall put them to death. If they do so in secret then I will cut them off.
Therefore shall ye keep my charge. This charge. The charge being not to do [any of these abominable practices].
The meaning of which were done before you is, a person shall not say, since the earlier ones did so, I will also do so.
I am Hashem your Elokim is connected to My charge. One who lacks intelligence shall not ask, “Why this charge?” For I am Hashem your Elokim. Do all that I command you.

[Unto all the congregation of the children of Yisrael.] The reason that Scripture states unto all the congregation of the children of Yisrael is to exclude strangers since they, like Bnei Yisrael, are commanded to abstain from prohibited sexual relations.

The reason this chapter follows the one dealing with prohibited sexual relations is that Bnei Yisrael should not imagine that they would remain in the land by observing only the laws dealing with the prohibited sexual relations. Hashem informs them that there are other commandments. If they do not observe them, they will be exiled from the land. The aforementioned are the ten statements. Hashem warns against idol worship after stating, I Hashem…am holy which, according to many commentators, is parallel to the first statement of the Decalogue. And ye shall not swear by my name falsely (v. 12) is parallel to Thou shalt not take the name of Hashem thy Hashem in vain (Shemot 20:7).

And ye shall keep my sabbaths. This parallels Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy (Shemot 20:8). Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father is similar to Honor thy father and thy mother (Shemot 20:12). Neither shalt thou stand idly by the blood of thy neighbor (v. 16) is likewise the same as the statement Thou shalt not murder (Shemot 20:13). The law regarding the bondmaid designated for a man (v. 20) is parallel to Thou shalt not commit adultery (Shemot 20:13 with a free woman. Similarly, Ye shall not steal; neither shall ye deal falsely, nor lie one to another (v. 11); Thou shalt not oppress thy neighbor (v. 13) are parallel to the three remaining statements. I have previously told you in my comments on the Torah portion Ve-Elleh Ha-Mishpatim (now these are the ordinances) (Shemot 21:1) that each and every precept stands by itself. However, there is some support for connecting the verses. Note, the section that opens with the words Ye shall be holy (v. 2) begins with Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father (v. 3). Now Scripture tells us that the years of the one who honors his parents will be long (Shemot 20:12). This implies that the days of one who disrespects his parents will be shortened. Scripture therefore says, Ye shall fear. The reason Scripture mentions the mother before the father is that a child first recognizes only its mother. Then it recognizes its father. The Torah next mentions the Sabbath because, unlike all the other festivals, a child is commanded to keep the Sabbath. The child shall then recognize his Elokim who rested on the seventh day. Scripture next mentions, Turn ye not unto the idols (v. 4). We know from tradition what Scripture means by fearing parents. Our verse employs the word ish (every man) once because it wants to be brief. Scripture employs the plural tira’u (ye shall fear) because those who observe the child have to teach him and force him to fear his parents. It is the same case regarding Sabbath observance.
The meaning of I am Hashem your Elokim is, act as I did, for I rested from all work on the Sabbath.
Turn ye not. Even in your hearts to look upon them.

Unto the idols. The reference is to statues. They are called elilim because they are false objects. Compare the word elil (no value) in Ye are physicians of no value (Iyov 13:4). It is possibly related to the word al (not). Elilim means things that do not exist.

Nor…molten gods. Made to receive power from those who are on high, for there is no need for another god along with Me. Scripture therefore states, I am Hashem your Elokim. Scripture employs the plurals tifnu (turn ye) and ta’asu (make), for the one who sees idol worship and does not reveal the matter is a partner of the idolater.

And when ye offer a sacrifice of peace-offerings. This is connected to what is written above. It means that one shall not sacrifice to the demons, no-gods, but only unto God. Scripture employs the plural tizbechu (ye offer), for Scripture is speaking about what is most prevalent, for people to join together to offer a sacrifice.
Scripture reads li-retzonekhem (that ye may be accepted) because they shall not be forced to bring the offering but shall offer it of their own free will.
But every one that eateth it. The meaning of okhelav is every one that eats of it. Similarly But the righteous are secure as a young lion (Mishlei 28:1).

Because he hath profaned the holy thing of Hashem. After he offered the parts designated to Hashem by Scripture, all the flesh is holy. Chillel (profaned) is related to the word chol (profane). It is something that has no significance. It is like an empty space (challel). In this section Scripture explains the punishment, namely, and that soul shall be cut off.

[And when ye reap the harvest.] This follows the law dealing with the peace offering, for as you gave to Hashem the parts designated in Scripture, so shall you, out of respect for Hashem, give what Scripture designates from the harvest of your land for the poor and the stranger. The word u-ve-kutzrekhem (and when ye reap the harvest) is grammatically irregular. It is an infinitive in the kal.
The corner of thy field. The Yisraeli shall leave a corner in the field.
The gleaning. The meaning of leket (gleaning) is known.

Glean. Te’olel (glean) means to cut off the olelot, that is the young grapes. Compare, olel (young child). Very young children are also called yonekot (sucklings). This word is similar to shereshkha (root thee out) in And root thee out of the land of the living (Tehillim 52:7), the meaning of which is, to cut the root. Similarly the meaning of mesa’ef purah (Is. 10:33) is to lop the boughs.
The fallen fruit. The meaning of peret (fallen fruit) is known in the words of tradition. It is related to the word poretim (thrum) in That thrum on the psaltery (Amos 6:5).
For the poor. Of Yisrael.
And for the stranger. Who lives among you.

[Ye shall not steal.] Ye shall not steal follows, for Scripture, as it were, says I have commanded that you give from your property to the poor out of respect for Hashem. You shall certainly not take what belongs to others.
Scripture employs the plural Ye shall not steal, for the one who sees and is silent is also a thief.
Neither shall ye deal falsely. This applies to something which has been deposited with you. The one who knows and does not testify also deals falsely.
Nor lie. Seek money from one who does not owe you anything.

[And ye shall not swear by my name falsely.] This follows Ye shall not steal, for the one who is suspected of theft and dealing falsely with regard to a deposit swears. Scripture employs the plural ye shall not swear because it wants to include the one who causes an oath to be taken.
Scripture reads, so that thou profane the name of thy Hashem because, as I have noted, the one who swears falsely denies Hashem.
Thou shalt not oppress thy neighbor. In secret.
Nor rob him. Openly by the use of force.

The wages. Pe’ulat means the wages of. Compare, Behold, His reward (u-fe’ulato) is with Him (Is. 40:10). It is possible that Scripture is elliptical and that pe’ulat is short for sekhar pe’ulato (the wages of his labor). Many say that Scripture speaks of a person hired for the day. One is not permitted to tell him to work the next morning and in the morning say I will pay you for two days’ work. The transmitters of tradition say that our verse refers to someone hired for a day, for the sun is not permitted to set on a worker who is hired for the night.
[Thou shalt not curse the deaf.] Because you have the power to do so. You shall likewise not put a stumbling block before the blind.
But thou shalt fear thy Elokim. For He is able to punish you and make you deaf and blind.
Ye shall do no unrighteousness. Scripture speaks of the judges and the witnesses.
The person of the mighty. Great in money such as Barzilai (Shmuel II 19:33).

A talebearer. The word rakhil (talebearer) is similar to rekhulltekh (thy merchandise) (Yechezkel 26:12) and rokhel (merchant) in With all powders of the merchant (Cant. 3:6). Rakhil means a slanderer, for the merchant moves goods. He buys from one person and sells to another. The talebearer reveals to one person what he heard from another person.

Neither shalt thou stand idly by the blood of thy neighbor. A person should not join bloodthirsty men. It is known that many people have been murdered and killed because of slander. Doeg the Edomi is proof of this.
The meaning of I am Hashem is, I see what you do in secret.

Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thy heart. This is the reverse of but thou shalt love thy neighbor (v. 18). Now all of these commandments are implanted in the heart. Yisrael will dwell in the land when they observe them, for the second temple was destroyed because of hatred of one’s neighbor for no reason.
Thou shalt surely rebuke thy neighbor. Perhaps you suspected him of something which was not so. The meaning of and not bear sin because of him is that you be punished because of him.
Thou shalt not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge. This is explained in the words of our rabbis of blessed memory.

But thou shalt love thy neighbor. Many are of the opinion that the lamed of le-re’akha (thy neighbor) is superfluous. It is like the lamed of le-avner (Avner) (Shmuel II 3:30). I believe that le-re’akha is to be taken literally. Its meaning is that one should love that which is good for one’s neighbor as he does for himself.
The meaning of I am Hashem is, I Hashem alone created all of you.

[Thou shalt not let thy cattle gender with a diverse kind.] The reason Scripture states Thou shalt not let thy cattle gender with a diverse kind is to warn us. Since you are holy, in that you do not act violently towards your fellow human being, you must also not do anything to an animal which entails changing Hashem’s work. Scripture therefore reads, Ye shall keep My statutes; that is, each species is to be preserved. A kind is not to interbreed with another kind.

With a diverse kind. Kilayim (a diverse kind) means two kinds. I will yet explain the meaning of kilayim. The reason for the law regarding a field and a garment is that they serve as reminders, for many commandments serve as reminders. Examples of the latter are: the festival of unleavened bread, Sukkot, tzitzit, shofar, mezuzah, and tefilin. I will hint to you here at a secret. Know that “the complete is very complete.” Scripture therefore says with regard to Avraham, and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws (Bereshit 26:5).

Of two kinds. The transmitters of tradition said that the word shatnez (two kinds) is made up of three words. It may come from a five-letter root. The meaning of shatnez is “mixed.” It is a noun which stands alone in Scripture.

A bondmaid, designated for a man. The deniers say that the bondmaid is not a Jewess. However, the correct interpretation according to the plain meaning of the text is that the bondmaid is the one mentioned in And if a man sell his daughter to be a maid-servant (Shemot 21:7) and that she is a Yisraeli. Our verse deals with an instance in which the bondmaid was designated for marriage to her master or his son. However, she had not undergone the first stage of marriage. The meaning of nor was freedom given her is that she is not free until she undergoes the first stage of marriage as is the practice of young ladies.

Many believe that necherefet means designated. However, I believe that necherefet is related to the word cherpah (reproach) because she is an unmarried virgin maidservant under the control of a stranger.
Redeemed. Hofdeh (redeemed) is an infinitive in the hofal. The meaning of and not at all redeemed is that her father or any other family member did not redeem her before she became a young woman.

Freedom. The shuruk in chufshah (freedom) is in place of a furtive kamatz, for the individual form of the word is chofesh. Scripture states, nor was freedom given her, because it was traditional to write a writ of manumission if her father sold her for a set time. The transmitters of tradition said that our verse speaks of a woman who was half free and half servant. What they said is true.

There shall be an inquisition. Some say that bikkoret (inquisition) means a concubine. They say that the same applies to the word biykkrotekha (among thy favorites) in Kings’ daughters are among thy favorites (Tehillim 45:10). However, they did not explain it correctly, for the meaning of biykkrotekha is, among the precious handmaidens. The yod is missing because the bet, which serves as a preposition, is vocalized with a chirik. It is vocalized with a chirik because of the confluence of two mobile shevas, the first beneath the prefix and the second beneath the first root letter of the word yikkrotekha, which is in the feminine. The tongue does not have the power to enunciate two mobile shevas in succession. The same is true for the entire language. There is no exception to this except for the word mi-yeshene (that sleep) in And many of them that sleep in the dust (Daniel 12:2), according to the reading of Ben Naftali. There are those who say that bikkoret is related to the word yevakker (seek) in shall not seek (Vayikra 13:36). The meaning of bikkoret is that the matter shall be searched out. The transmitters of tradition say he incurs the penalty of being lashed with a strap made from the skin of cattle (bakar). This is true by way of tradition. The word bikkoret is used as a support for the tradition. This section is placed here because the one who sleeps with the bondwoman oppresses the master of the bondwoman. He therefore brings a ram as a guilt offering. Furthermore, this type of intercourse can be interpreted midrashically as mixing diverse kinds, namely, a free man and a bondwoman.

And he shall be forgiven. I will explain this later. The reason Scripture now discusses forbidden fruit is that Scripture had previously mentioned the seed of the field and the seed of the woman, who is likened to the ground. Scripture therefore now mentions that which is planted. It is known that fruit which grows before three years have passed is of no value and is harmful to the body. It is like all fish that have no fins and scales that are injurious to the body,0 and like all flesh of birds of prey and unclean animals that harm the wise soul. The intelligent will understand this.

[Then ye shall count the fruit thereof as forbidden.] The meaning of ve-areltem et orlato (then ye shall count as forbidden) is that the fruit is counted as a foreskin which is harmful and serves no purpose, such as the “foreskin” of the lips, the ear, and the foreskin of the penis.
The meaning of ve-areltem (then ye shall count) is, you shall consider it as a foreskin. It is also beautifully explained in the Aramaic translation.
Shall it be as forbidden
Unto you. This explains the meaning of ve-areltem (then ye shall count).
Shall be holy, for giving praise. For giving praise to Hashem. The kohen shall eat it.

[That it may yield unto you more richly the increase thereof.] That it may yield unto you more richly the increase thereof is connected to shall be holy, for giving praise (v. 24) even though it is some distance from it. If he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft (Shemot 22:2) is similarly connected to he shall pay five oxen for an ox (Shemot 21:37). There are many other similar instances.
The meaning of I am Hashem your Elokim is, I will place a blessing upon the produce.

Ye shall not eat with the blood. This is connected to what is written above it. Scripture warned against eating from the fruit of any planted tree until the fifth year. It similarly also prohibited one, if he is in the proximity of the sanctuary, to eat from any permitted flesh unless its blood first be sprinkled on the altar of Hashem. The account of King Shaul is a faithful witness to this interpretation, for the ark of Hashem was with Shaul, and Scripture explicitly states, “Behold, the people are eating with the blood.” As I explained, it was as if the people were sacrificing to the demons, for this was their custom in Mitzrayim. There they were accustomed to sacrifice in the name of the demons. Now this is clear, since the blood was not poured on the altar in the worship of Hashem. Neither shall ye practice divination is connected to ye shall not eat with the blood because they used to eat with the blood and go astray after the demons in Mitzrayim, and they used to practice divination and soothsaying in Kenaan. The aforementioned is clearly stated in Scripture. This too was like the doings of the land of Mitzrayim;…and…the doings of the land of Kenaan (Vayikra 18:3). The word menachesh means divines. Compare, I have observed the signs (nichashti), And Hashem hath blessed me (Bereshit 30:27). Divinations take many forms. There are types of divination that employs images, sticks, actions, movements, days, and hours.

Soothsaying. Some say that the word te’onennu (soothsaying) is related to the word anah (answer). The soothsayer imagines something in his heart and inclines his ear to hear what the speaker will answer. However, the rule of grammar rejects this interpretation. There are those who say that te’onennu comes from the word onah (time). It is similar to the word onatah (her conjugal rights) in and her conjugal rights, shall he not diminish (Shemot 21:10). However, it appears to me that te’onennu is related to the word anan (cloud), for it is known that the one who practices divination looks at the clouds and observes their forms and their movements. Te’onennu probably comes from a verb with a doubled root. It is like the word tesovevu (you will go round about), for we find, And with soothsayers (onenim) like the Plishtim (Is. 2:6). [I note this] for it is possible that te’onennu is a doubled form. Me’onen (one that uses divination) u-menachesh (Devarim 18:9) is proof.

[Ye shall not round the corners of your heads.] Scripture states, Ye shall not round the corners of your heads as the non-Jewish nations do, so that you will be separated from them. Now since the hair on the head and the beard serve to glorify a person it is unfit to destroy them. Some say that this verse is connected to Ye shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead (v. 28), for there are people who destroy the hair on the corner of their heads and also on the corner of their beards for the dead.
Cuttings. We know the meaning of the corners of the head and of the beard from the words of tradition.
The word le-nefesh means for a dead body. It is also so rendered in the Aramaic translation. This is its true meaning. The nun does not receive a dagesh in order to simplify enunciation.

Imprint any marks. Some say that this is connected to Ye shall not make any cuttings in your flesh, for there are people who, employing fire, mark their bodies with a recognizable form for the dead. Even today there are those who, while young, mark their faces so that they [may] be recognized. The word ka’aka (marks) is doubled. Compare, He that spread forth the earth and that which cometh out of it (ve-tze’etza’ehah) (Is. 42:5). Ka’aka is related to the word ve-hoka (and hang) in and hang them up (Bamidbar 25:4). According to the Aramaic translator, it is also an irregular word. He is also correct [in translating ka’aka as engraved].

[Profane not thy daughter.] Scripture now mentions profane not thy daughter because it earlier stated Ye shall not make any cuttings in your flesh (v. 28). The import of our verse is, your daughter shall not be displayed before the public. Now the voice of a woman is like her nakedness. A cutting is certainly so.
Lest the land fall into harlotry. The reference is to the harlotry of the people of the land. Compare, when a land sinneth against Me (Yechezkel 14:13).
[Ye shall keep my sabbaths.] Scripture now says, Ye shall keep My sabbaths, because it earlier dealt with the dead, for there is no mourning on the Sabbath.
And reverence My sanctuary is to be understood as referring to the kohen gadol; he shall not act as other mourners do. There is a similar prohibition upon all the people of the sanctuary.

The meaning of I am Hashem is, Hashem will punish you if you do not revere the sanctuary and respect it. Scripture similarly next mentions the ghosts and the familiar spirits (v. 31) because of the dead. It similarly writes in Yeshayahu on behalf of the living unto the dead (Is. 8:19).
The ghosts. Ovot (ghosts) is related to the word ovot (wineskins) in Like new wine-skins (Iyov 32:19), for wineskins are the main instruments in this “art.”

Nor unto familiar spirits. Yidonim (familiar spirits) is related to the word da’at (knowledge). Those who turn to yidonim seek to know the future. The empty heads say if there were no truth in the ovot (ghosts) and in various magical practices, then Scripture would not have prohibited them. However, I say the reverse. Scripture would not have permitted that which was true. It only prohibited that which is false. The idols (elilim) and the images (v. 4) are proof of this. Were it not that I do not want to go on at length, I would have explained the incident of the woman who was an expert in divining by ghosts. I would have brought unquestionable proof to my explanation.
The meaning of Turn ye not is, do not turn to the one who knows the art.
The meaning of seek them not out is, do not inquire of them as king Shaul did.

The meaning of I am Hashem your Elokim is, you shall not seek except for Hashem alone. Note, Scripture reads, to be defiled by them, because the soul of the one who inquires of a ghost or a familiar spirit is defiled, for it does not cleave to Hashem.

[Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head.] Scripture mentions the hoary head because it earlier mentioned the dead and the aged are close to death, for the bodies of the old are considered dead. Note, our verse refers to all the old and to every hoary head.
The meaning of and thou shalt fear thy Elokim is, fear the Lord who shall punish you in your old age.

And if a stranger soujorn with thee. Scripture mentions the stranger after the old man. It does so to, as it were, to say, as I warned you to respect the old Yisraeli because he has no strength, I warn you not to wrong the foreigner because you are stronger than he is, or who has no power because he is in your country and subject to you.
And thou shalt love him as thyself. This has been explained.

[Ye shall do no unrighteousness.] Scripture states, Ye shall do no unrighteousness because it earlier dealt with the stranger. Our verse is similar to and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him (Devarim 1:16). You shall similarly not cheat in measurements; that is, you shall not deceive in measuring cubits, for the cubits vary. It is also possible that the meaning of in judgment is according to the known practice of the land.
Just balances, just weight. Avne tzedek means just weights.
A just ephah. For that which is dry.
And a just hin. For liquid. A just hin explains in measure (v. 36).

Scripture states, I am Hashem your Elokim, who brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim, because it earlier mentioned for ye were strangers in the land of Mitzrayim (v. 34). Therefore, you are obligated to keep My statutes and ordinances in mind and observe them.
The meaning of I am Hashem is, you shall pursue my statutes which I placed upon you, for they are all righteous.

[And Hashem spoke unto Moshe, saying.] Scripture earlier stated, unto all the congregation…of Yisrael, because the commandments, which followed, are obligatory upon all of Yisrael. Strangers have no part in them. Scripture now begins to mention the punishment for harlotry, which will befall anyone who lives in the Land of Yisrael, be he native born or resident alien. It begins with the most severe of them all, namely, with the individual who gives of his seed to Molech, that is, the one who has intercourse with a woman who worships idols.
The meaning of the people of the land is, the people of the land wherein the culprit resides, be he a native or a resident stranger. This applies to one who publicly offers his offspring to Molach.
I also will set my face against that man. If the sin was committed secretly. Others say that the reference is to the extirpation of the culprit’s seed.
To defile my Sanctuary. Which is in the Land of Yisrael.
And to profane my holy name. For nations will hear.
