It would have appeared to us that ba-even (with stones) (v. 2) is a collective noun. Compare, And I have oxen (shor), and asses (chamor) (Bereshit 32:6). However, the words of tradition are correct. They are true. Rabbi Yonah the Spanish grammarian who rests in paradise says that and against his family (v. 5) means all those like him. Who brought us into this trouble? Our verse is to be taken literally. The people of the land will hide their eyes because they are of his family.
[And all that go astray after him.] This means others will go astray if the culprit is not put to death.

And the soul that turneth unto the ghosts. This means as I will cut off the one who gives from his seed to Molech in secret or in public if the people of the land do not kill him, so will I cut off the one who strays from me and turns to ghosts. We find the term nefashim (souls) (Yechezkel 20:13) in Scripture. We also find all the souls (nefesh) were fourteen (arba’ah asar) (Bereshit 46:22). We similarly read, and will cut him (oto) off.

Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy; for I am Hashem your Elokim. Ki ani Adonai Elohekhem (for I am Hashem your Elokim) means for I Hashem your Elokim am holy. I have given you statutes to observe in order to sanctify you. Scripture has already mentioned this. It repeats this command so as to include the strangers residing among Yisrael, for they too are obligated to be holy so that they may continue to be allowed to dwell in a holy land.

Scripture begins the list of punishments at the beginning of the section with the person who curses his father in the same manner that Scripture earlier starts with Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father (Vayikra 19:3). Our verse mentions the father before the mother out of respect for the father. It is unlike Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father, for he is not put to death if he has not reached the age of mitzvah observance.

For whatsoever man there be that curseth his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. The phrase asher yekallel (that curseth) is to be read as if written twice. Our verse is to be read as if written, “and whoever curses his mother.” He hath cursed his father or his mother is another way of saying he has committed a great abomination.

His blood shall be upon him. Compare, his blood shall be upon his head (Yehoshua 2:19). The blood of those who are stoned and strangled is upon them. I will now state a general rule concerning all executions. We cannot derive the manner of execution from Scripture. Hence we need the tradition of our fathers. Scripture similarly does not state at what age one is obligated to observe the commandments.

[And the man that committeth adultery with another man’s wife.] Scripture next mentions, and the man that committeth adultery with another man’s wife, for she was prohibited. The meaning of even he that committeth adultery with his neighbor’s wife is similar to he hath cursed his father or his mother (v. 9). It means he committed an evil act.
And the adulteress. Women who are raped would not be so termed.
He hath uncovered his father’s nakedness. He has committed a great sin.
His daughter-in-law. Kallato means his daughter-in-law.
Corruption. I have previously explained the meaning of tevel (corruption).
Both of them have committed abomination. If the one who was penetrated was not raped.
And if a man take with his wife also her mother, it is wickedness. Zimah (wickedness) means a promiscuous thought.
And they. This one or that one. If the mother was his wife, then the daughter is burned. The same is true in the reverse.
And ye shall slay the beast. So that it not cause another to sin. Others say, to hide the shame.

And lie down thereto. Le-rivah (and lie down thereto) is an infinitive even though it is vocalized with a chirik, for the forms of the infinitive change. Compare, be-shivri (when I break) (Vayikra 26:26).
And if a man shall take his sister, his father’s daughter. In a place where he is unknown and afterwards the facts become known.
The meaning of and see her nakedness is, or see her nakedness. It is like he hath cursed his father or his mother (v. 9). See means uncover.
The meaning of and she see his nakedness is that they both agreed to this.

It is a shameful thing. The word chesed (shameful thing) is related to yechassedkha (revile thee) in Lest he that heareth revile thee (Mishlei 25:9). Chesed hu (it is a shameful thing) means it is an inflated act of harlotry.
He hath uncovered his sister’s nakedness. Employing force.

He shall bear his iniquity. He alone shall bear his iniquity. The reason scripture mentions these things regarding the sister is that they grew up in one house and are young people who play. The brother is always alone with his sister. Scripture does not mention the punishment for intercourse with the daughter of one’s son or the daughter of one’s daughter, for it relied on the oral Torah. It is possible that they are not mentioned because of the father’s lack of desire, for he is advanced in years when he has a mature daughter. It is for this reason that Scripture does not mention the mother of one’s father and the mother of one’s mother, for they are aged.
Sickness. She is ill because of her blood.
And shall uncover her nakedness means that he committed a great abomination.
The meaning of and she hath uncovered is that she willingly uncovered, for if she was forced to have intercourse the man alone is cut off.

And…the nakedness of thy mother’s sister. Its meaning is, I have previously warned you not to uncover the nakedness of thy mother’s sister. Now the one who uncovers the nakedness has made naked his near kin.

They shall bear their iniquity. If they willingly acted thus. Scripture does not mention the punishment for having intercourse with the sister of one’s father. It also does not even hint at the punishment for taking two sisters. The intelligent will understand why. The words of tradition are also true.
With his uncle’s wife. Dodato refers to his uncle’s wife.

They shall die childless. The Sadducees say that aririm (childless) means naked and that the meaning of yamutu (they shall die) is, they shall be put to death. They did not speak the truth. The correct interpretation is found in the words of the Aramaic translator, for aririm is similar to ariri (childless) in I go hence childless (ariri) (Bereshit 15:2). I have previously explained Write ye this man childless (ariri) (Yirmiyahu 22:30).

[It is impurity.] Scripture employs the term niddah (impurity) with regard to a brother’s wife. The meaning of niddah hiy (it is impurity) is, it is fitting for him to distance himself from her. Similarly, Your brethren that hate you, that cast you out (menaddekhem)…have said (Is. 66:5). Note, there is no mention of niddah in all of the prohibited sexual partners except with regard to a brother’s wife. A niddah is prohibited. However, a time comes when she is permitted. This possibility, as I will explain in the section If brethren dwell together (Devarim 25:5), also arises in the case of a brother’s wife. My reply to those who say, as it is prohibited to marry the sister of the father (v. 19) so it is prohibited for a woman to marry her uncle is: this is not the way of Scripture. It is the males who are dominant with regard to the prohibited sexual practices. No one dominates the male. Let those who accept the faulty logic of those who offer the above interpretation show us why we should not accept the testimony of two women. If they argue from the laws of evaluation then four women should be equal to two male witnesses. We therefore need tradition.
Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes. Not to violate the laws regarding these prohibited sexual practices.
And all mine ordinances. The laws governing the punishment of those who engage in prohibited sexual practices.
[Vomit you out.] I will explain this in the Torah portion Va-Yelech.
And therefore I abhorred them. This was stated metaphorically. Compare, and His soul were grieved (Jud. 10:16).
The meaning of a land flowing with milk and honey (v. 24) is, there is no land like it.
Who have set you apart from the peoples. With these statutes. Furthermore, Ye shall…separate between the clean beast…(v. 25).
[The clean.] The ten mentioned beasts. All the others are unclean.
The unclean fowl means the unclean fowl which are mentioned. All others are clean.

The meaning of to hold unclean is that you shall know in your mind and in your speech that it is unclean. Similarly, ye shall have in detestation among the fowls (Vayikra 11:13). A resident alien shall therefore not eat that which is unclean in the clean land. He shall dwell in the land on this condition.
If you keep all that I command you, you will then be holy. You are obligated to follow Me, for I the Lord am holy.

[A man also or a woman.] The reason Scripture states A man also or a woman that divineth by a ghost or a familiar spirit, shall surely be put to death is that the Torah earlier had said concerning ghosts and familiar spirits, seek them not out to be defiled by them (Vayikra 19:31). Scripture now says, be holy and put to death the one who defiles himself with a ghost or a familiar spirit. Previously it did not mention the punishment for publicly turning to a ghost. Scripture mentions woman, for this art is mostly practiced by women. Similarly, Thou shalt not suffer a sorceress to live (Shemot 22:17).

Speak unto the priests. After charging Bnei Yisrael, and the sons of Aharon who are included among them, to be holy, Hashem told the sons of Aharon that they are commanded to keep themselves from other things, for they are the ministers of Hashem. It is possible that speak unto the priests refers to the section which is mentioned above, for the Torah is in the hands of the kohanim.
And say unto them. This refers to the commandments which they alone are obligated to keep.
For the dead. Le-nefesh (for the dead) refers to the dead.
The word yittamma (defile) is a hitpa’el. The tet receives a dagesh because the tav is, swallowed.
The meaning of be-amav (among his people) is among all of Yisrael, who are his people.

Except for his kin. It had appeared to us that the meaning of she’ero (His kin) is similar to she’er (near of kin) in None of you…to any that is near of kin to him (Vayikra 18:6). In other words, she’ero is a general term, with the details for his mother, and for his father following.

The meaning of ba’al be-amav (a chief man among his people) (v. 4) is that a husband shall not defile himself for his wife. However, since we saw that our teachers transmitted to us the law that a kohen is permitted to defile himself for his wife, the first interpretation falls away. They employed the word she’er as a support, as I explained in my comments on the phrase unto a foreign people (Shemot 21:8). The rabbis said that the meaning of ba’al is, a chief who rules over the people, as in the owner thereof (be-alav) not being with it (Shemot 22:13). The reason Scripture mentions the mother of the kohen before the father is that in most cases the male lives longer than the female.

That is near unto him. In that she is his sister from his father and his mother. Now, aside from those mentioned, a chief (v. 4) shall not defile himself for any of his people, be they kohanim or Bnei Yisrael.
To profane himself. The lamed has a dagesh in it to compensate for the missing other lamed. Le-hechallo (to profane himself) is an infinitive in the nifal.
They shall not make baldness upon their head. Over the dead.
The corners of their beard. Over the dead, as is the practice in places in the land of the Kasdim. The meaning of the corners of thy beard (Vayikra 19:27) is thus clarified.

Saratet (cuttings) means even one cut. Yisrael has already been cautioned not to do these things. The reason Scripture warns the kohanim about this is that one who has a bald head, or whose beard has been shorn, or whose flesh is cut shall not serve before Hashem.
And not profane the name of God. The reason being, for the offerings made by fire…they do offer.

Woman that is a harlot. If we follow the plain meaning of the text then we do not find in all of Scripture the word zonah (harlot) to have any but its literal meaning. The meaning of and have given a boy for a harlot (zonah) (Yoel 4:3) is also as I have explained.

Or profaned. A woman who is not known as a harlot. According to the plain meaning, it would appear from the words of Yechezkel that the widow of a kohen is permitted to marry other kohanim. The words of tradition are thus true.
Thou shalt sanctify him therefore. In mind and in speech.
The bread of thy Elokim. Food which is offered to Elokim.
I Hashem, who sanctify you. All of you.

If she profane herself by playing the harlot. Many believe that techel (profane) is related to techillah (beginning). However, I believe that it is related to the word chillul (profane) but it is a hifil. Compare, he shall not break (yachel) his word (Bamidbar 30:3). According to both interpretations the word comes from a double root. However, it is irregular. It is possible that the word hechel (profaned) (Yechezkel 20:9) and the word techel are both irregular in that the tav is vocalized with a tzereh so that it not is confused in meaning with techillah (beginning). Similarly, hechel (profaned) in that it should not be profaned (Yechezkel 20:9).
And the daughter of any priest…she shall be burnt with fire. If she profaned herself by harlotry, for she profaned the honor of her father.
She shall be burnt with fire. Whether she is either married or betrothed.
The garments. The reference is to the holy garments.
Shall not let the hair of his head go loose, nor rend his clothes. We learn from this verse what our sages transmitted regarding the laws of mourning.

Neither shall he go in to any dead body. Nafshot met is to be read as if written nafshot guf met (dead body). The word guf (body) is missing, for met (dead) is an adjective. Similarly, But the rich answers impudent (Mishlei 18:23) and and their food plenteous (Chavakuk 1:16), where the word lamb is missing.
The meaning of he shall [not] go in is, he shall not go into a tent or a house where the dead body is located.

The meaning of for his father, or his mother is, for his father and mother, whom he is obligated to respect while they live and after their death. The kohen gadol may certainly not defile himself over his brother or his son.

Neither shall he go out of the Sanctuary. After the dead, so said the transmitters of tradition. What they said is correct. Some say that the reference is to the seven days of consecration. However, this cannot be so, for Scripture has already stated, and [the kohen] that is consecrated (v. 10). It is also possible that the meaning of our verse is that the kohen gadol shall not go out of the sanctuary except for the purpose of observing a precept.

In her virginity. There are nouns in Hebrew that never come in the singular. Compare, ne’urim (youth), zekunim (old age), alumim (youth), and betulim (virginity). There are other words which never come in the plural, i.e., taf (children), shekhem (shoulder), zahav (gold), and barzel (iron).
A widow, or one divorced. Any woman widowed or divorced from a kohen or a Yisraeli.
Or a profaned woman, or a harlot. The connective vav before the word zonah (harlot) is missing. Compare, The sun moon (shemesh yare’ach) stand still in their habitation (Chavakuk 3:11).
The reason Scripture reads but a virgin is that it wants to add of his own people, for a captive virgin and a convert are prohibited to him.

And he shall not profane his seed. By taking a widow or a divorced woman in secret. These shall he not take (v. 14) means he shall not publicly take any of these women. After Scripture mentions the sanctity of the kohanim it begins to list the blemishes.

The bread of his Elokim. The reference is to the sacrifices offered on the altar. The kohanim spoken of in our verse refer to common priests. Scripture therefore states anyone who is of the seed of Aharon the kohen.
Maimed. Charum (maimed) is the reverse of saru’a (too long). Note, charum is related to the word cherem (destruction).
Too long. Saru’a (too long) is related to the word me-histare’a (to stretch himself) (Is. 29:20).

Or crook-backed. The word gibben (crook-backed) is most probably related to the word gavnunnim (peaks) in ye mountains of peaks (Tehillim 68:17). The nun is a root letter. Gibben is an adjective. Similarly the word dak (a dwarf) is to be interpreted according to the plain meaning.
Dak means short of stature.

Hath his eye overspread. Some say that tevallul (overspread) is related to the word tevel (corruption) in they have wrought corruption (Vayikra 20:12). Tevallul means a corruption. Others say that tevallul is related to the word belullah (mingled) in mingled with oil (Vayikra 2:5). According to both interpretations the tav of tevallul is superfluous.
According to the opinion of many the scab (garav) is also in the eye.

Or scurvy. Yalefet (scurvy) means sticking. It is related to the word va-yilpot (took fast hold) in And Shimshon took fast hold (Jud. 16:29). There are others who say that yalefet means crooked. It is related to the word va-yillafet (turned) in that the man was startled, and turned (Rut 3:8). The yod of yalefet is superfluous. It is like the yod of yitzhar (oil) (Bamidbar 18:12).
Crushed. Mero’ach (crushed) is an adjective. It is related to the word ru’ach (wind).
Stones. Ashekh (stones) refers to the testicle. After listing specific blemishes the Torah issues a general statement and says, no man…that hath a blemish (v. 21).
The meaning of hath a blemish is similar to he hath cursed his father or his mother (Vayikra 20:9).
The bread of his Elokim…of the most holy. The showbread, the guilt offering, and the sin offering, which in comparison to the peace offerings are most holy, for the peace offerings are also holy.
And of the holy. The tithe and the first-born.
Only he shall not go in unto the veil. Although he is a kohen gadol. He shall also not approach the altar.

[And unto all the children of Yisrael.] If it were not for the tradition we would interpret and unto all the children of Yisrael as meaning that those who are blemished should not slaughter peace offerings for the children of Yisrael. Now, since Scripture mentions that a blemished kohen may eat that which is holy, it warns that the one who eats sacred food must be clean.

That they separate themselves. Ve-yinnazeru (that they separate themselves) is similar to ve-hizzhartem (thus shall ye separate) (Vayikra 15:31). Ve-yinnazeru is a nifal. It means they shall distance and separate themselves. It is related to the word nazir (nazirite).

And that they profane not. And that they profane not applies to what immediately follows it and to what follows later. Our verse is to be read as follows: And that they profane not My holy name, and that they profane not that which they hallow unto Me.
The meaning of I am Hashem is, I Hashem am holy.
[From before me: I am Hashem.] This means since he is cut off from Hashem, he will cease to exist. I have explained the latter in my comments on the secret of Hashem’s name.
Until he be clean. Until the days necessary for his cleansing have passed.
Whereby he may be made unclean. The word lo means whereby. Compare the word li (of me) in say of me: He is my brother (Bereshit 20:13). All those mentioned shall become unclean until evening.

And when the sun is down, he shall be clean. It is known that he shall be clean refers to the unclean, for there is no mention of the word day in the verse. Compare, and the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean (Vayikra 12:8). However, the rabbis of blessed memory transmitted to us the law that even if the sun sets he shall not eat until it is completely dark. They used this verse as a support. I have explained the latter in my comments on the verse unto a foreign people (Shemot 21:8). The rabbis therefore said that ve-taher (he should be clean) means that the day shall be clean.
Because it is his bread. His food. I have previously explained this.

Those whose brains are empty explain the verse in Yechezkel, which reads, The priests shall not eat of any thing that dieth of itself, or is torn, whether it be fowl or beast (Yechezkel 44:31), as meaning that the priests shall not eat anything brought down or torn by animals or fowl. However, this is nonsense, for the Torah states all that dies of itself or is torn he shall not eat. The meaning is if he eats he shall not minister.
They shall therefore keep my charge. Mishmarti (my charge) alludes to the sanctuary. Scripture therefore reads, lest they bear sin for it (alav), and die therein (vo).
There shall no common man. One who is not of the seed of Aharon.
They may eat of his bread. Males and females.
That which is set apart from the holy things. The thigh and the breast (Vayikra 10:15).
She may eat of her father’s bread. As at first.
But there shall no common man eat of it. The reference is to a son, if she has one. She cannot eat of the holy food because of her son.

And shall give unto the priest the holy thing. The meaning of ve’et ha-kodesh (the holy thing) is, with the holy thing. On the other hand, and shall give unto the priest might apply to what precedes it and to what follows it. Our verse is to be interpreted as follows: Then he shall put the fifth part thereof unto it and shall give it unto the priest, and he shall give unto the priest the holy thing. I believe that there is no need for this interpretation, for Scripture reads unto it.
And so cause them to bear. Ve-hisi’u (and cause…to bear) is a hifil. Its meaning is, they shall caution them and teach them so that they do not err.
After mentioning the holy things of the children of Yisrael Scripture goes on to caution Bnei Yisrael to not bring the holy things from blemished animals.

[Strangers.] Scripture reads or of the strangers for it is stated that there is one law for the Yisraeli and the stranger who offer a vow or freewill offering. The sages differentiated between a vow offering and a freewill offering. All vow offerings are freewill offerings. However, not all freewill offerings are vow offerings. It is fitting that all sacrifices that are offered in their entirety on the altar be unblemished.
Clearly uttered. Le-fale means to clearly utter.
Blind. Avveret (blind) is an adjective relating to the eye.

Some say that shavur (broken) means a break in the hand and charutz (maimed) refers to an injury in the foot. Charutz is related to charatzta (hast decided it) in So shall thy judgment be; thyself hast decided it (Melachim I 20:40). Charutz means cut.
A wen. Yabbelet (wen) is similar to tevallul (overspread) (Vayikra 21:20). The general rule is: we rely on tradition, not on our deficient minds.
Ye shall not offer these unto Hashem. In fulfillment of a clearly uttered vow. Nor shall the kohen take the organs from these.

Too long. Saru’a (too long) has the same meaning as when first mentioned (Vayikra 21:18). TOO SHORT. Kalut (too short) is the opposite of saru’a (too long). Kalut is related to the word miklat (refuge) in the city of refuge (Yehoshua 21:13).
Bruised. Ma’uch (bruised) is related to mo’akhu (pressed) in their bosoms pressed (Yechezkel 23:3).
Or crushed. Katut (crushed) is related to va-ekkot (beat) in and beat it in pieces (Devarim 9:21). Crushed and bruised refer to wounds in the testicles.
Or torn. Natuk (torn) is related to yinnatek (broken) in as a string of tow is broken (Jud. 16:9).
Neither shall ye do thus in your land. To change Hashem’s work.
From the hand of a foreigner. One should not think as follows: I will not hesitate to offer this sacrifice, for it is the offering of a foreigner.

Their corruption. The mem of moshchatam (their corruption) is not a root letter. However, its tav is a root letter. Moshchatam is related to the word hashchatah (destruction). On the other hand, the mem of moshchatam (their anointing) (Ex.40:15) is a root letter and the tav is not.

Be accepted. Yeratzu (be accepted) is a nifal. After stating that a blemished sacrifice will not be accepted, Scripture goes on to say that any sacrifice brought from an animal less than eight days old will also not be accepted.

When a bullock, or a sheep, or a goat. The newborn animals are called by what they ultimately become. Compare, And stripped the naked of their clothing (Iyov 22:6); “the dead shall be put to death” (Devarim 17:6); “for the one who falls shall fall from it” (Devarim 22:8). On the other hand, Scripture may have been referring to the name of the species.
[But from the eighth day and thenceforth.] Like a child that is circumcised, that is, until a quarter of the month has passed.
Thenceforth. Hale’ah (thenceforth) means afterwards. The arrow of Jonathan is proof.
And whether it be cow or ewe. I have previously explained this. The commandment pertains to both males and females.

[And when ye sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving.] The reason that And when ye sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving…On the same day it shall he eaten follows is that Scripture earlier noted it is prohibited to kill a cow or a ewe [and its young together] in one day. Scripture adds to what is written in the Torah portion Tzav (Vayikra 6:2), that ye may be accepted.
[I am Hashem.] Scripture reads I am Hashem to teach that the thanksgiving offering is to be “whole.”
And ye shall keep my commandments. In your hearts.
And do them; I am Hashem. For I investigate what is in the heart, and I see everything that is done.

[And ye shall not profane my holy name.] This is directed to the sons of Aharon, for this section is connected to what is earlier stated. They are commanded not to sacrifice for themselves or for Yisrael a cow and its offspring on one day. It is also possible that And when ye sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving (v. 29) is directed to the kohanim. The fact that the following section opens with Speak unto the children of Yisrael (Vayikra 23:2) is proof of this. But I will be hallowed among the children of Yisrael is a second witness.

That brought you out. The verse ends with I am Hashem. This the first statement of the Decalogue and the root of all the commandments. After mentioning the holy things of the children of Yisrael, the Torah notes the days that Yisrael shall offer burnt offerings. It starts with the Sabbath.
[Even these are my appointed seasons.] Scripture reads, even these are My appointed seasons (mo’adai) because there are many Sabbaths in the year.
In all your dwellings. In your country and outside of your country, at home and on the way.
I have previously explained the meaning of it is a sabbath unto Hashem.

Scripture then mentions the festivals (v. 4). The Torah says, even these are My appointed seasons, with regard to the Sabbath and in their appointed season with regard to the festivals. The meaning of in their appointed season is, in any day of the week in which they fall. Note, I will now lay down a general rule with regard to the festivals. During the time of the Temple the festivals were in the hands of the Beth Din. Do you not see that Scripture says, For the king had taken counsel (Divrei Hayamim II 30:2), with regard to the Passover proclaimed by Chizkiyahu. After Chizkiyahu established the new moon of Nisan he proclaimed a leap year. Our sages, of blessed memory, criticized him for this, for he should not have added a Nisan on Nisan. The transmitters of tradition said that the Beth Din took many things into consideration in estabhshing the year. They said, regarding Rabbi Akiva, that he established two leap years back to back according to the needs of the hour. There is no proof in Scripture as to how Yisrael established the months and the festivals. The Gaon’s statement to the effect that they relied on the intercalational calculation is not true, for there are proofs in the Mishnah and also in the Talmud that Passover fell on a Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. There are also two stories in the Talmud [which show that they did not rely on a fixed calendar]. Leap years come close to compensating for the additional days which a solar year has over a lunar year. The latter does not follow the way of the ancients. The calculation starts with the end of 14 hours of the sixth day; that is, add four days, eight hours, and 876 parts to five hours and 204 parts of an hour of the second day of the week. Then the birth of the new moon will occur at the end of 14 hours of the sixth day. A year is added, for we start counting from five hours and 204 parts of an hour of the second day of the week because of the five days which preceded the creation of Adam, for a day into a year is considered a year. This presents no problem. You cannot add an additional year, for it did not yet exist. Note, an additional month was added to the year after a year and a half. The intercalation is based on the average movement of the moon. The sages therefore said that sometimes the birth of the moon comes at longer intervals; at times it comes at shorter intervals. The establishment of the month is not tied to the sighting of the moon in Yerushalayim, or in the far east, or in the west [of the world]. The place of the average conjunction of the moon is proof of this, for look, it is reckoned when occurring over Yerushalayim. Furthermore, we have seen the moon many times on the second night of the month of Nisan. It was similarly seen in the entire world. However, the month was established on the third night [of the week]. The same thing happened in the three months preceding Nisan. This occurs when the birth of the new moon of Tishrei occurs at nine hours and 204 parts of an hour of the third day [of the week]. It was enacted because of the postponement. There are also times when the month of Tishrei was established on the fifth day [of the week] and the moon was not seen on the night of the Sabbath. Now, the air was then clear. This occurs every year when the birth of the new moon is close to half of the day and the moon is in half of its sphere’s apogee. The establishment is also not dependent on the time of the conjunction of the sun and moon. It is not even dependent on their mean conjunction, for note, the conjunction of the sun and moon at 15 hours and 599 parts of the hour on the second day and similarly the conjunction at nine hours and 204 parts of the third day is proof of this. If I did not want to go on at length I would explain the secret of the calculation of the calendar and the secret of the very difficult law, i.e., the rule regarding a moon born before midday. The general principle is: our wise men, of blessed memory, transmitted to us the rule that we are to rely on the intercalated calendar in exile. We received the same from the mouth of the prophets. We cannot do anything better than it. The sages ruled that the festivals be observed for two days in the Diaspora because of uncertainty. Those who fast for two days in observance of Yom Kippur fast in vain due to the “postponements.” For in a year when the birth of the new moon occurs at nine hours and 204 parts of the hour on the third day of the week, they should fast on what is the eighth day of the month according to our calculation if they rely on the conjunction. Why manipulate the date of the start of one year because of another year? This would happen to them if the month is established by seeing the new moon.
At dusk. I have previously explained this.
An offering made by fire. These are described in the Torah portion Pinechas.

Scripture reads, When ye are come into the land (v. 9), so that Yisrael would observe all the Sabbaths in the wilderness and the Passover at Mount Sinai. This section was given close to the [time of the] erection of the tabernacle.
[Speak unto the children of Yisrael.] This means speak unto the children of Yisrael and tell them to gather. Afterwards, say unto them…

On the morrow after the Sabbath. The sages said that on the morrow after the sabbath means on the morrow after the festival. Those who contradict the sages say that the word Sabbath is be taken literally. Those who believe in the Rabbinic tradition offer proof from the Sabbatical year, the Jubilee, the great fast, and the day of shofar sounding, for the word shabbaton (a solemn rest) is employed with regard to them. Scripture similarly employs shabbaton with regard to Sukkot and Shemini Atzeret. They also say that the meaning of sheva shabbatot (v. 15) is seven weeks. The same is true of ba’eh shabbat im yotze’eh shabbat (those that were to come in on the sabbath, with those that were to go out on the sabbath) (Melachim II 11:9). The same word is employed with two meanings in one verse. Note, we find a similarity in sheloshim ayarim (thirty ass colts) (Jud. 10:4). They offer proof from the word complete (v. 15). A wise man in Rome offered proof from on the morrow after the passover, unleavened cakes and parched corn (Yehoshua 5:11). He did not know that it cost him his life, for the Passover falls on the 14th and the morrow following it is on the 15th. Scripture similarly reads, And they journeyed from Raamses in the first month (Bamidbar 33:3). The eating of parched corn is prohibited until the waving of the omer. The Gaon says that there are two Passovers, a Passover of Hashem and a Passover of Yisrael. The Passover of Hashem is on the night of the 15th. Now, the day after the Passover in Yehoshua refers to the 16th day. It follows from this that the interpretation of on the morrow after the passover (Bamidbar 33:3), is on the morrow following the sacrifice of the Passover. What he said has no value. The festival is called Passover only because Hashem skipped over the houses. Its morrow is the morning of the 15th. Scripture similarly writes, all that day, and all the night, and all the next day (yom ha-mochorat) (Bamidbar 11:32). The Gaon further states that the unleavened cakes and the parched corn were from the old grain. This is not far-fetched, for Scripture says that the waving of the omer should begin from the time the sickle is first put to the standing corn (Devarim 16:9). If the omer was waved on the 15th when did they harvest and make unleavened bread? Furthermore, there was no harvest, for the omer is brought from the first of the barley harvest. There is also what appears to be proof of the Gaon’s opinion, for Scripture states, of the produce (meavur) of the land (Yehoshua 5:11). It is possible that the term avur refers to the produce of the year that has passed. The meaning of the produce of the land is the produce of the land of Sichon and Og. The fact that Scripture afterwards states, of the fruit of the land of Kenaan (Yehoshua 5:12), is proof. Furthermore, kaluy (parched corn) (Yehoshua 5:11) is not the same as kali (parched com) (Vayikra 23:14). Now, Scripture says, And ye shall eat neither bread nor parched corn (kali), nor fresh ears (v. 14). The verse which reads kaluy ba-esh (parched with fire) (Vayikra 2:14) cannot serve as an argument to the contrary, for it describes the act since corn in the ear parched in fire is called kaluy. We can also ask: From where do we know that the kohen waved the omer on the other side of the Yarden, for the verse states, which I give unto you (v. 10)? However, the land was not yet given to them. Scripture mentions matzot and corn only because the manna ceased. This is the meaning of the entire verse. The Gaon further says: If the word Sabbath is to be taken literally then from which Sabbath shall we start to count? Yehoshua answers that there are 18 days aside from the Sabbath whereon sacrifices are offered. These days are called mo’adim (festivals). Now, since there is a sacrifice on the day that the omer is offered it is a sign and a witness that the waving takes place on one of the days of the spring festival. Note, he forgot the sacrifices that are offered on the new moon, which are not mentioned. Furthermore, Scripture states, After this manner ye shall offer daily, for seven days (Bamidbar 28:24). Scripture should have stated, aside from the offering of the omer. This too is no argument against us, for we rely on tradition when it comes to the commandments. Now, Scripture does not state “aside from the he-lambs brought for a peace offering,” when it lists in the Torah portion Pinechas the offerings to be brought on the festival of Shavu’ot. It states above, and one young bullock, and two rams (v. 18). However, Pinechas reads, two young bullocks, one ram, seven he-lambs of the first year (Bamidbar 28:27). The believer can also answer that Moshe prophetically knew the day that the omer would be waved. He knew that the first day of the month would be established on the Sabbath. The arrangement of the bread which took place on the Sabbath is proof of this. Scripture notes how they calculated the first year. They then brought the peace offerings and the burnt offerings which are mentioned [in our Torah portion] and then the ones mentioned in the Torah portion Pinechas. Scripture then goes on to say, in your feast of weeks (Bamidbar 28:26) and seven weeks (Devarim 16:9); it does not state Sabbaths. There is no proof that the beginning of the week starts with the first day. In fact, then she shall be unclean two weeks (Vayikra 12:5) shows that this is not the case. Look, I will hint at a secret. All the festivals are contingent on a specific day of the month. Scripture does not give a date for the festival of Shavu’ot because of the counting, which is a commandment. The rabbis, of blessed memory, transmitted the tradition that the Torah was given on the festival of Shavu’ot and that it is concerning this day that Scripture states, for we must hold a feast unto Hashem (Shemot 10:9).

Some say that whenever the Torah uses the term li-retzonekhem it means to be accepted from you, for Scripture reads, And he shall wave the sheaf before Hashem, to be accepted for you (li-retzonekhem) (v. 11). The meaning of the aforementioned is that you shall wave it willingly. This means you shall offer a he-lamb of the first year so that you will be accepted.

Those who deny the Rabbinic tradition say that ben shanah (of the first year) (Shemot 12:5) does not have the same meaning as ben shenato (of the first year), for ben shanato refers to a lamb under a year and ben shanah refers to a lamb of a complete year. Note, they did not read the section dealing with the dedication of the altar. The latter reads, one he-lamb of the first year (ben shenato), for a burnt offering (Bamidbar 7:15). However, in the final section it reads, the he-lambs of the first year (bene shanah) twelve (Bamidbar 7:87).
Bread. From the new grain. The fact that the Passover offering is eaten with matzot and bitter herbs is proof of this.

If it were not for tradition it would have appeared that the counting of the days is similar to the counting of the years of the Jubilee. Those who deny the Rabbinic tradition say that the meaning of complete is that the first Sabbath from the morrow on which the count begins is not to be considered in the count.
Shall ye number fifty days. For this is the way the Torah counts. Similarly, in all cases of the eighth day.
[Ye shall bring out.] The word tavi’u (ye shall bring out) is irregular in that its alef has a dagesh in it. We do not know the reason for this.
Of your dwellings. We need tradition to teach us from which place it was brought and when it is to be brought.
Two wave-loaves. For the kohen along with the peace offering lambs.

It is possible that Scripture changed the sacrifices in the first year because it was the beginning of the beginning. Some say that the kohen shall offer either a bullock and two rams or two bullocks and one ram. It depends on the will of the kohen. We do not find such a commandment again. I will give its true explanation in the Torah portion Pinechas.

Now, since the slaughtering of the peace offerings took place on the festival of Shavu’ot and it is a day of holy assembly, it is thus permissible to slaughter on all the festivals. The latter is contrary to the opinion of the Sadducees.

[And when ye reap.] The reason Scripture mentions And when ye reap the harvest of your land… a second time is that Shavu’ot is the festival of the first-fruits of the wheat harvest (Shemot 34:22). Scripture cautions: Do not forget what I commanded you to do at this time.

[Spoke.] The reason the statement And Hashem spoke precedes the law dealing with the day of the sounding of the shofar is that the latter is a festival unto itself. However, the festival of Shavu’ot is connected to the day the omer is waved. And Hashem spoke is similarly written in connection with the great fast and the festival of Sukkot.

In the seventh month. We begin the count of months from Nisan, for we then left Mitzrayim. Furthermore, the festival of the new ears of barley comes first, next come the first-fruits of wheat harvest (Shemot 34:22), and then the time when you gather in the produce of your work (Devarim 16:13). These festivals are contingent upon the days that are mentioned.

Scripture commands that trumpets are to be sounded on all new moons. It follows from the aforementioned that zikhron tru’ah (a memorial proclaimed with the blast of horns) and yom tru’ah (a day of blowing the horn) refer to the sounding of a shofar. Similarly, on Yom Kippur. I will hint at some secrets to you. Pay attention. Perhaps you will understand them. The transmitters of tradition said that Rosh Ha-Shanah is a day of judgment and that the sounding of the shofar proclaims the kingdom of Hashem. Now, since the new moon is the most important [day of the month], the first month of Nisan is the most glorious month because the tabernacle was erected then. Yechezkel in speaking of the future says, In the first month, in the first day of the month (Yechezkel 45:18). Similarly, And so thou shalt do on the seventh day of the month (Yechezkel 40:20) because of the quarter. Note, the 15th day of the month corresponds to the time when one half of the month faces the other half. The seventh day is also a quarter. On the second Passover the great and the small interchange. The day of Rosh Ha-Shanah is therefore greater than all of them. Now, even though it is the Day of Judgment it is prohibited to fast on it. The Book of Ezra shows that this is the case. On Yom Kippur the small light is in the conjunction. Note, Sukkot is like Passover. However, its eighth day, not its seventh, is a festival. From this, the secret and the secret of the Sabbath will become clear to you.

[Howbeit.] Scripture reads, Howbeit on the tenth day, because a day of solemn assembly (v. 24) is a joyful day. The Book of Ezra similarly reads, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet (Nechemyah 8:10).
And ye shall afflict. I have previously explained the meaning of afflict.
To make atonement for you. Its meaning is, it is a day of atonement for you alone.

For whatsoever soul it shall be that shall not be afflicted. Te’unneh (be afflicted) is a pu’al. This is a sign that if we know of a person who does not observe this precept as we observe it, then we shall force that individual to fast. The reason Scripture says that no manner of work is to be done on Yom Kippur is so that people will not be engaged in anything but seeking atonement for sins.
That soul will I destroy. There is a difference between “destroy” and “cut off” (v. 29). I cannot explain the difference.
[No manner of work.] Scripture repeats, Ye shall do no manner of work, in order to add, it is a statue for ever throughout your generations.
Shall ye keep your Sabbath. Scripture reads your sabbath, for the Sabbath day is not called the Sabbath of Yisrael but the Sabbath of Hashem.
Seven days ye shall bring an offering made by fire. Even though it is not the same as the offering made by fire that is brought on Passover.

It is a day of solemn assembly. Some say that atzeret (solemn assembly) means an assembly as in azteret bogedim (an assembly of treacherous men) (Yirmiyahu 9:1). Azteret refers to the gathering of all of Yisrael on the three pilgrimage festivals. However, they did not speak correctly, for look, Scripture states with regard to Passover, and on the seventh day shall be a solemn assembly (atzeret) (Devarim 16:8). However, it also states and thou shalt turn in the morning, and go unto thy tents (Devarim 16:7). It appears that atzeret is similar to netzar (detained) in detained before Hashem (Shmuel I 21:8). Atzeret means that the Yisraeli shall not be involved in any worldly affairs. The meaning of atzeret is, ye shall do no manner of servile work. Scripture writes similarly with regard to the atzeret of the festival of Passover.

These are the appointed seasons of Hashem. Whereon you are obligated to bring an offering made by fire. Scripture explains that on all of these festivals a burnt offering, a meal offering, a sacrifice, and libations are to be brought, for until now Scripture only mentioned an offering made by fire, and it is possible that an offering made by fire refers only to a burnt offering or only to a meal offering.
And beside your gifts. On the three pilgrimage festivals. Similarly, And the vows of the congregation and of the individual and their freewill offerings.

[Howbeit.] Scripture reads howbeit because it mentioned the affliction of the soul in the preceding section. The Torah prohibited fasting on the festival of Sukkot, for Scripture reads with regard to this festival, And thou shalt rejoice (Devarim 16:14)…and thou shalt be altogether joyful (Devarim 16:15).
When ye have gathered in the fruits of the land. From the fields and vineyards.
Ye shall keep the feast. Tachoggu (ye shall keep the feast) comes from a double root. The reference is to the sacrifices.

On the first day shall be a solemn rest. Shabbaton (a solemn rest) is a noun. The words “shall be unto you” are missing. If shabbaton were an adjective, the word yom (day) would have a heh rather than a bet prefixed to it.

And ye shall take. We shall believe in the words of the transmitters, for they do not contradict Scripture. The latter is so even though we find, they shall take to them every man a lamb (Shemot 12:3). They also transmitted to us the tradition that the fruit of goodly trees (v. 40) refers to the etrog (citron). In truth, there is no fruit of the tree more beautiful than the etrog. The rabbis interpreted the phrase etz hadar (goodly trees) to mean [a fruit] which dwells on its tree. They used the verse as a support for their tradition. I have explained the latter in my comments on to sell her unto a foreign people (Shemot 21:8). The Sadducees say that the sukkah shall be built from these plants. They brought proof from the Book of Ezra. However, they are blind of heart. Do they not see that the Book of Ezra does not at all mention willows of the book and fruit of the tree? It only mentions the leaves of five kinds of branches. The mention there of myrtle branches and branches of thick trees is no argument against our ancients. Similarly the kind called myrtle does not grow on a tall tree. There are thus two kinds, one growing on a tall tree and one on a low tree. The person who wanders from the land of Kedar to the land of Edom will know the secret of this commandment if he has eyes.

That…in booths. Bnei Yisrael made booths after they crossed the Sea of Reeds. They certainly did so in the wilderness of Sinai, where they dwelt close to a year. This is the manner of all the camps. This festival too is thus in memory of the Exodus from Mitzrayim. Should someone ask why this commandment is to be observed in the month of Tishrei, then one can answer: Hashem’s cloud was over the camp during the day and the sun did not strike them. However, they started to make sukkot from the days of Tishrei onwards because of the cold.

Unto the children of Yisrael. Not to all of the children of Yisrael, for Moshe could not talk to all of them. Scripture similarly reads, Speak unto the children of Yisrael. (verses 2, 10, 24, 34). The verse unto all the congregation of the children of Yisrael (Vayikra 19:2) is no argument to the contrary, for all of Yisrael is not called a congregation.

[Pure olive oil.] The reason Scripture now mentions the section dealing with the pure olive oil is that the Torah earlier recorded the fire offering of each festival and now has to mention the show bread. The menorah stood opposite the table.

[Upon the pure candlestick.] Scripture in our section adds upon the pure candlestick. The latter refers to the known candlestick, which was constructed by Betzalel and was completely made of gold. It does not refer to any other candlestick. [As to the menorah], which was made of iron, it was done so in time of need by the word of the prophets.
And thou shalt take fine flour. By command. Similarly, and bake…thereof. Ve-afita (and shalt bake) is ultimately accented. It is irregular.
In two rows. Corresponding to the number of the tribes. This is similar to the secret of the ephod and the breastplate. The two tenth parts (v. 5) corresponded to the arrangement of the two rows.
Upon the pure table. In contrast to the other tables that were there. This table alone was covered with gold and its crown was of gold.

It was the frankincense that was with the bread that served as an offering made by fire unto Hashem. The bread was for the kohen. It is possible that Scripture mentioned this section because there is an obligation on Yisrael to provide the festival burnt offerings, the oil, and the bread, which was always on the altar.
For Aharon and his sons. His entire household.
And the son of an israelitish woman…went out. From his tent. Compare, came out, and stood at the door of their tents (Bamidbar 16:27).
Whose father was a Mitzri. Who converted to Judaism.

And a man of Yisrael. Ve-ish ha-yisra’eli (and a man of Yisrael) is similar to le-ish he-ashir (unto the rich man) (Shmuel II 12:4) and to et yom ha-shevi’iy (the seventh day) (Bereshit 2:3). We do not know why this section was connected to that which comes before it. Perhaps the blasphemer spoke improperly with regard to the bread, the oil, and the sacrifices.

Blasphemed. Some say that the meaning of va-yikkov (blasphemed) is enunciated. Compare, Which the mouth of Hashem shall mark out (yikkavennu) (Is. 62:2) and that are pointed out (nikkevu) by name (Bamidbar 1:17). Others say that va-yikkov is similar to ekkov (I curse) in How shall I curse (Bamidbar 23:8). However, I believe that the first interpretation is correct.
In ward. In a known place in the camp.
And let all that heard. For he was stoned because of their testimony.

All the congregation. The reference is to the magnates of the land who are the great ones of Yisrael. Some say that Whosoever curseth his God (v. 15) means whosoever curseth his God in secret. The correct interpretation is as follows. The term Elokim (god) is an adjective. The angels are called elohim. So are the judges. Who can know what is in the mind of the one who curses? However, if he enunciates the glorious name of God, which stands by itself and is not an adjective and is not intertwined with any noun, [he shall be stoned]. Its meaning is, when one curses and enunciates the Name he shall be put to death if he enunciates the Name as the son of the Mitzri did. The Name is not mentioned out of respect for God. Scripture reads, as well the stranger, as the home-born…shall be put to death. It is possible that the ones who quarreled (v. 10) struck each other. This section was therefore written. It had previously been mentioned. However, our chapter adds, as well for the stranger, as for the home-born (v. 22).[17. AND HE THAT SMITETH.] Scripture begins with and he that smiteth any man mortally. He is not participating in war and deliberately smites any man, be that man a stranger or a native
And he that smiteth a beast mortally shall make it good. Note, the phrase life for life, serves two verses.
So shall it be done to him. Shimshon said, so have I done unto them (Jud. 15:11).

The Gaon brought proof from logic that breach for breach (v. 20) cannot be taken literally. The first wound was made unintentionally. How can we justify making a similar wound? If the wound is in a vital area, the person will die. The same applies to the eye. How are we to do the same to one who injured his neighbor by causing him to suffer the loss of a third of the sight of an eye? The words of tradition are thus true. Scripture is to be understood as follows. Ransom money is to be paid in all of these cases. It is fitting to remove his eye if he does not ransom it. Should one argue against us and say, what happens if the injurer is poor? Then we answer, Scripture speaks about the majority of cases. It is possible for the poor to become rich. This also answers those who argue, what shall we do in instances when the injurer of the eye is blind? SO SHALL IT BE RENDERED UNTO HIM. There are instances where the bet has the meaning of on. Compare, the beast that I rode upon (bah) (Nechemyah 2:12). There are many such instances. On the other hand, its meaning might be, so shall it be rendered unto him if he does not pay ransom.

[And he that killeth a beast.] Scripture repeats And he that killeth a beast… because it wants to mention the stranger, for when Scripture speaks of maiming (v. 19) it speaks of a Yisraeli, for the Torah clearly says, his neighbor. However, there is one law for both the stranger and the native regarding he that kills a person and he that kills a beast.I have previously informed you that Scripture is being brief when two cafs come together. Scripture also chooses to employ brevity when it does not add “and he dies” to u-makkeh adam (and he that killeth a man), for it is known that the culprit is not executed unless the one who is struck dies. Another interpretation for the repetition is that Scripture earlier mentions “mortally” (v. 17). The latter refers to a blow struck in a vital area. Scripture then lays down the following general law: A person who kills shall be put to death whether the blow was struck in a vital area or in a non-vital area. The word nefesh (mortal) is thus not mentioned.
[Your Elokim.] The Elokim of the native and the Elokim of the stranger.
And the children of Yisrael did. They did from this day and onward to one who injures his neighbor, in accordance with this law.

In Mount Sinai. There is no chronological order in the Torah. This section precedes, And the Lord called (Vayikra 1:1) and all the sections that follow it, for the words recorded in our section were told to Moshe on Mount Sinai. Moshe now made the covenant recorded in the Torah portion Now these are the ordinances (Shemot 21:1). Moshe inserted this portion at this point to place in proximity the conditions under which Bnei Yisrael could dwell in the land. He said that the land would spit out Bnei Yisrael if they violated the laws of prohibited sexual relations. He said a similar thing in the Torah portion If ye walk in My statutes (Vayikra 26:3) with regard to the Sabbaths of the land. Moshe first mentions the Sabbaths.

Then shall the land keep a Sabbath unto Hashem. There is a commandment upon the Yisraeli not to allow a stranger to sow in the Sabbatical year. This is similar to the commandment that we not allow a stranger to do work on the Sabbath. Scripture commands this, for the stranger is in our power.
A sabbath unto Hashem is similar in meaning to the Sabbath day. The secret of the days of the world is alluded to in this place.
The produce thereof. Of the land mentioned in the first verse.
A Sabbath of solemn rest. I previously explained the meaning of shabbat shabbaton (a Sabbath of solemn rest).

That which groweth of itself. It is known that the word safi’ach (that which groweth of itself) is connected to the word sefacheni (put me) in Put me, I pray thee (Shmuel I 3:36). It is also known that the word nezirekha (undressed vine) is related to the word nazir (nazirite).
A year of solemn rest. Its meaning is, because it is a year of solemn rest for the land; that is, the land is not in your possession in this year.
And the sabbath-produce…shall be for you. Sabbath-produce refers to all that the land brought out by itself.
The meaning of lakhem (for you) is, for everyone.
The meaning of lekha (for thee) is that the owner of the field is permitted to eat of that which grows of itself.
And for thy cattle. Which are under your control.
And for the beasts. Which are not under your control.

Then shalt thou make proclamation with the blast of the horn. There is a difference of opinion as to whether the world was created in Nisan or in Tishrei. There is no need to dwell on this, for the transmitters of the law ordained that we are to say in the Rosh Ha-Shanah prayer which they established for us, “This day marks the beginning of Your works, it is a memorial of the first day.” We also read in Scripture that the shofar is to be sounded in the Jubilee year in the month of Tishrei at the beginning of the year. Furthermore, the Torah, in the portion commanding the people to gather to hear the Torah read states that the Torah is to be read on the festival of Sukkot. Scripture writes, that they may hear, and that they may learn (Devarim 31:12). It is not possible for this to take place after half a year has passed. Furthermore, Scripture states, and the feast of ingathering, at the end of the year (Shemot 23:16). Similarly, and the feast of the ingathering at the turn of the year (Shemot 34:22). The faithful proof is the Sabbatical year, regarding which it is written, ye shall not sow (v. 11). They start sowing in the month of Marcheshvan in the Land of Yisrael. If the beginning of the year started in Nisan, then they would not harvest that which they sowed in the sixth year and they would not sow, for it is the Sabbatical year. Since they will not harvest what they planted in the sixth year, they will not sow twice. However, Scripture states that they should not sow in the seventh year alone. Yehudah Ha-Parsi said that Yisrael employed a solar calendar. Now if this were so [then we do not know the exact time that a year begins] for, note, Moshe did not explain the length of a complete year and so far the astronomers are unable to bring the length of a solar year to light. For example, the wise men of Hodu add a fifth of an hour to the quarter of the day. Ptolemy and his friends say that 1/300 of the day is missing. This is close to that of the intercalated calendar. Those who came after him said one part of 106. Others said 110. Still others said 130. There are those who say 180. For there are those who calculate the year when the sun concludes a cycle around the constellations from a visible point. Others calculate it from a point on the sphere which inclines to the right and the left. We need tradition. Furthermore, the meaning of the word chodesh (month) contradicts the Parsi. The Sadducees say that the Jewish religion is based on a lunar year. Note, there is no year at all to the moon. However, as the sun has no months, the calculators sought a number of months close to that of a solar year. They found them to be 12. The calculators sought a number of days for the month that would be close to the number of days into which a lunar month is divided. Our months are therefore lunar months and our years return at the end of a solar year. Our sages therefore transmitted to us a law given to Moshe from Sinai that the Bet Din always made seven leap years in every cycle even though they used to establish every month by sighting the moon. The secret of the cycle is known from the science of the stars.
The meaning of shall ye make proclamation is that they should sound the shofar in all the roads.
And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year. All the inhabitants with regard to working the land.

Liberty. The meaning of the word deror is known. It means liberty. As the flying swallow (deror) (Mishlei 26:2) refers to a small bird that produces music when it is free. However, if it is taken captive it refuses to eat and starves to death.

Jubilee. The word yovel (Jubilee) means sent. The sages, of blessed memory, said that the meaning of yovel is a lamb. Shoferot ha-yovelim (rams’ horns) (Yehoshua 6:4) is proof of the latter. The year is called by the name of the shofar.
[Be unto you.] To Bnei Yisrael alone.
And ye shall return every man unto his possession. As Scripture goes on to explain, in the year of Jubilee the land that is sold shall return to its owners.
And ye shall return every man unto his family. The servant sold to a Yisraeli.
A jubilee shall that fiftieth year be. Since it is the year of Jubilee you shall not sow.
It shall be holy unto you. For it is distinguished from the other years.
Ye shall eat the increase thereof out of the field. You shall eat what the land produces of itself. It is the same as is written regarding the Sabbatical year.
In this year of jubilee. Its meaning is in the beginning of the year.

Or buy. Kanoh (buy) is an infinitive. A word is missing. Kanoh is in place of kenitem kano (you will surely buy). Compare, zakhor (remember) in Remember the sabbath day (Shemot 20:8). There are many such instances. The word timkeru (thou sell) is in the plural because it shall be sold in front of witnesses. The same is true of al tonu (ye shall not wrong).
[According to the number of years.] Only according to the number of years.
Thou shalt increase the price thereof. The reverse of thou shalt diminish.
[And ye shall not wrong one another.] This is to be understood as a warning to the seller, for the first injunction is directed to the buyer.

For I am Hashem your Elokim. As I am your Elokim, I will exact punishment from the two of them, from the one who wrongs his neighbor. If you observe My statutes the earth will bring forth its produce. Scripture mentions this because it earlier spoke of the number of crops (v. 16).

[Our increase.] The Sadducees say that our increase proves that the year begins in Nisan. This is no proof, for it is possible that the meaning of our increase is what the earth produces of itself. If they say that what the earth produces of itself is not called tevu’ah (increase) but safi’ach, then ye shall eat the increase thereof (tevu’atah) out of the field (v. 12) contradicts them. Furthermore, let them inform us how Bnei Yisrael were to act in the Jubilee year, for they would not sow in the sixth, seventh, and eighth year. They would only sow in the ninth year and harvest in the tenth. Why didn’t Scripture mention this, for Scripture only mentions for the three years (v. 21). It appears to me that the meaning of and it shall bring forth produce (v. 21) is, I will place a blessing on the sixth year that it will be sufficient for the sixth and an additional year. However, in the Jubilee year there will be food for three years and no more.

[And it shall bring forth.] The word ve-asat (and it shall bring forth) is irregular. Compare, ministered (mesharat) unto the king (I Rings 1:15). Scripture reads thus because it drops one of the tavs to simplify enunciation when two tavs are joined.

The old store. The word yashan (the old store) adverts to the word min (of). The meaning of min (of) is, of the very thing. Similarly, with (min) the ark-cover shall ye make the cherubim (Shemot 25:19).

In perpetuity. The word tzemitut (perpetuity) is similar to keritut (divorcement) (Is. 50:1). The tav is a root letter. Tzemitut is related to the word yatzmitem (will cut them off) in Hashem will cut them off (Tehillim 94:23).

For the land is mine. This is an important reason. Moshe similarly said in his prayer, Hashem, Thou hast been our dwelling-place (ma’on) (Tehillim 90:1). [The meaning of the latter is, Hashem, You are like a permanent dwelling-place. However, One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh (Kohelet 1:4).
The land of your possession. Which you inherited in the land of Kenaan. Also in the land of the Emori.
Be waxen poor. Yamukh (be waxen poor) comes from a root which consists of two stem letters that are sounded and one silent letter placed between them. Its meaning is poor and destitute.
That is next unto him. From his family.
Then let him count. The word ve-chishav (then let him count) is a pi’el.

It shall go out. That which is sold shall go out. Note, a noun is used in place of an adjective. There are many such instances. Since Scripture states a dwelling-house in a walled city (v. 29), we know that and sell some of his possession (v. 25) refers to a field or a vineyard.
In a walled city. A city surrounded by a wall.

A full year. The word yamim means a year. Yamim means until the days return to their point of departure after completing their cycle of cold and hot, summer and winter, for the return of the sun to its place is the cause of this cycle. Now, we need tradition as to what determines a full year, whether it is a solar year, or a lunar year, or an intercalated year.
Shall be reckoned with the fields of the country. Al (with) in our verse is similar to al (and) in And they came, both men and (al) women (Shemot 35:22). The meaning of al is with.

They may be redeemed. The reference is to each and every house. Compare, Its branches (banot) run (tza’adah) over the wall (Bereshit 49:22), and for her children, (baneha) Because they are not (enennu) (Yirmiyahu 31:15).
A perpetual right of redemption. Olam (a perpetual right) means forever.

Scripture reads, va-asher yigal (and if a man purchase) (v. 33), because our verse reads ge’ulat olam. The meaning of yigal is shall purchase. There are those who say va-asher yigal means even if the redeemer is a Levi. The vav of ve-yatza (then…shall go out) (v. 33) has the same meaning as the unaspirated fa in Arabic. A house and a city (v. 33) have one law.

And his means fail. The word u-matah (and…fail) is related to the word yimmot (he shall…be moved) in he shall never be moved (Tehillim 112:6). The mem is a root letter. Similarly, the word matah (slippeth) in If I say: My foot slippeth (Tehillim 94:18).
Thy brother. A Yisraeli.
With thee. For you are obligated to the one who is found with you, the one that you see.
Then thou shalt uphold him. The reverse of and his means fail (matah). You shall uphold him so that he does not fall.
As a stranger and a settler. If he is from your country or is a stranger and a settler.
Shall he live. Va-chai (shall he live) means he shall live.

Interest…or increase. These terms are explained in the words of tradition. The tav of tarbit (increase) is superfluous. It is like the tav of tarmit (deceitful) (Tzefanyah 3:13). Tarbit is related to the word rav (many). However, it is a verb that comes from a root whose last letter is silent and hidden. It is similar to the word takhlit (utmost) in utmost hatred (Tehillim 139:22). Scripture next explains the terms neshekh (increase) and tarbit (increase). The mem of marbit (increase) (v. 37) is also superfluous. It is like the mem of maskit (figured) in any figured stone (Vayikra 26:1).

[I am Hashem your Elokim, who brought you forth out of the land of Mitzrayim.] Where you were strangers. Note, I gave you an inheritance. Our verse is connected in meaning to as a stranger and a settler shall he live with thee (v. 35). It is also connected to the already mentioned section, for it deals with the redemption of the land. Scripture mentions the section containing and his means fail with thee (v. 35) because it will go on to state that a Yisraeli who is in such great need that he sells himself shall go out in the year of Jubilee. All the sections of the Torah portion are thus connected.
And sell himself unto thee. He sells himself to you or he stole from you and he was sold by the Bet Din.
He and his children with him. The transmitters of tradition based themselves on this verse when they explained the meaning of and he shall serve him for ever (Shemot 21:6).
[For they are my servants.] Because I bought them from the house of bondage.
Thou shalt not rule over him. Tirdeh means you shall rule.
With rigor. Be-farech (with rigor) is to be explained as the Aramaic translator does.
Of the nations that are round about you. Such as Amon, Moav, Edom, and Aram.

Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you. Who dwell in the land of Kenaan, which is your country, and they are from the nations that are mentioned. Or the reference is to Mitzrayim and every nation aside from the seven nations, for Scripture commanded regarding the aforementioned, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth (Devarim 20:16). Note, it is prohibited to even feed them. It is possible that when the sages, of blessed memory, spoke of a Kenaani slave they spoke of someone who lived in Kenaan, not of a person of Kenaani ancestry. On the other hand, it is possible that the sages were able to ascertain the truth of the matter, for our mind is insignificant when measured against their minds.

And ye may make them an inhertance. Ve-hitnachaltem (and ye may make them an inheritance) is a hitpa’el. Similarly, ve-hitavvitem (and ye shall mark out a line) in and ye shall mark out your line (Bamidbar 34:10).
Of them may ye take your bondmen for ever. One is permitted to do so. However, since we find that the sages say that it is a commandment to do so, we accept what they say.
[But over your brethren the children of Yisrael.] Its meaning is, you will make a difference between your brother and the stranger.

Or to the offshoot. Eker (offshoot) means a root. The reference is to a person who accepted the Jewish religion. He himself is from the family of a stranger. The word eker has no neighbor. However, it is similar in meaning to ve-shereshkha (and root thee out) (Tehillim 52:7). It means the opposite of its stem. Similarly, te’akker (thou shalt hough) in thou shalt hough their horses (Yehoshua 11:6).

Or if he be waxen rich. He found a lost object or he inherited the money of a deceased member of his family. Scripture first mentions the brother and the family because that is what is most usually the case.
Him that bought him. Konehu (him that bought him) has the same meaning whether spelled with a heh or not.
He sold himself. Himakhero (he sold himself) is an infinitive in the nifal. The years that he was with his master shall be like the days of a hired man.

[If there be yet many years.] The vav in If there be yet many years…and if (ve-im) there remain but few years (v. 52) is like an unaspirated fa in Arabic. It means whether the remaining years be many or few.
According unto them, he shall give back the price of his redemption. It shall be so considered with regard to the money that he was bought for.
As a servant hired year by year. This is repeated in order to add that which follows. HE SHALL NOT RULE WITH RIGOR OVER HIM IN THY SIGHT. We shall not permit the stranger to rule over him with rigor.
And if he be not redeemed by any of these means. The years remaining until the Jubilee. Others say by those mentioned earlier.
For unto me the children of Yisrael are servants. This means you shall inform the stranger who buys a Yisraeli as a servant that the children of Yisrael are My servants.

Ye shall make you no idols. Scripture speaks of a Yisraeli who was sold to a non-Jew. It therefore warns the Yisraeli against the worship of idols. He (the Yisraeli slave) must not serve his master in anything relating to an idol. The Yisraeli shall also not serve his master on the Sabbath. The foreigner can purchase a Yisraeli only under these conditions.

And reverence my Sanctuary. By coming to the sanctuary during the three pilgrimage festivals. It is possible that Scripture states Ye shall make you no idols because Scripture had earlier stated, they are My servants (Vayikra 25:55). Now, since they are My servants they shall serve Me alone and not other gods.
Neither…a graven image. The meaning of pesel (a graven image) is known.
Or a pillar. For a graven image.

Figured. Maskit (figured) is a noun. It is similar to marbit (increase) (Vayikra 25:36). Maskit refers to a stone with figures on it. It is related to the word maskiyyot (imaginations) in the imaginations of their heart (Tehillim 73) and sekhiyyot (imagery) in delightful imagery (Is. 2:16).
Neither shall ye place…in your land. This is the way pagans worship Mercury.
For I am Hashem your Elokim. You shall bow to Me. It is so explained in the Yerushalayim Targum.
Ye shall keep my sabbaths. The Sabbatical years.

And reverence my Sanctuary. The year of Jubilee, for Scripture clearly states, it shall be holy unto you (Vayikra 25:12).I believe that Scripture employs My sabbaths in the sense of And from one sabbath to another, Shall all flesh come to bow before Me (Is. 66:23), for Scripture mentions to bow down unto it (v. 1). The meaning of Ye shall keep My sabbaths is you shall come every Sabbath to bow before Me, and not to a stone with figures on it. You shall come to My sanctuary alone. Note, Scripture mentions the chosen day, for this day, as I have previously noted, was chosen for the worship of Hashem. Scripture also mentions the chosen place.
The meaning of for I am Hashem is, for I rested from all work on the Sabbath and My glory dwells in the sanctuary. Scripture therefore says and reverence.
If ye walk in my statutes, and keep…and do. This is a commandment to study, to teach, and to observe.

[Then I will give.] The vav in ve-natati (then I will give) is like the vav in ve-ha’aretz (now the earth) in Now the earth was unformed and void (Bereshit 1:2). When a word which has a vav prefixed to it is ultimately accented, the word is an imperfect. When it is penultimately accented it is in the perfect. The above is, aside from a few instances, always the case.

Her produce. The word yevulah (her produce) is related to the word vul (food) in Surely the mountains bring him forth food (Iyov 40:20). We do not know whether the yod in yevul is a root letter or is like the yod in yekum (living substance) (Gen.7:23), which is not a root letter.
Threshing shall reach unto the vintage. Note, when thou gatherest in thy labors out of the field (Shemot 23:16) is now explained as meaning from the field and the vineyard.
Ye have enough. Sova (enough) is an infinitive.

Safely. La-vetach (safely) has the same meaning whether spelled with a lamed or not. The same is true of the word levadad (alone) (Bamidbar 23:9). Note, Scripture mentions sova (enough) first, for that is most important.

Scripture states, and dwell in your land safely, because people wander from their place in days of famine. Its meaning is similar to it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a wanderer shalt thou be (Bereshit 4:12).
And I will give peace in the land. Among yourselves.
And none shall make you afraid. No evil beast and no enemy. On the contrary, you will chase your enemies and they shall fall before you.

The greater wonder shall be that a small number of you shall pursue a large number of your enemies. I have previously informed you in my book Moznayim that ten, one hundred, a thousand, and ten thousand are round numbers. It is customary for one who magnifies a number to say “one to ten.” Compare, but thou art worth ten thousand of us (Shmuel II 18:3). Scripture here mentions that a hundred shall be chased by five. Note, Scripture doubled the number used by the one who magnifies. Each one of a hundred Bnei Yisrael shall chase a hundred of their enemies. There are those who say that Scripture adds to the number because the number is increased when the individuals come together. Similarly, How should one chase a thousand (Devarim 32:30). There is no need for this.
And your enemies shall fall. This is stated a second time. The repetition indicates that they will fall time after time. They will not rise again.

And I will have respect unto you. To greatly increase your wealth, to make you fruitful, and to multiply you with sons and daughters. It appears to me that and make you fruitful is the reverse of the barren womb (Mishlei 30:15).
And will establish my covenant with you. In that you will be as the stars of heaven for multitude (Deut.1:11) and as the dust of the earth (Bereshit 13:16).

And ye shall eat old store long kept. Amazingly, even though you shall be numerous there shall be so much produce that whoever will want to, shall eat from the old store and also from the old store long kept, which is older than the old store. The word noshan (long kept) is a nifal. There will be those who shall remove the old store from their house to make room for the new produce, for they will have no place to store it. There is a commentator who says that the meaning of and ye shall bring forth is you shall take it out to the field.

And I will set my Tabernacle. You will not fear that you might ever lack anything, for My glory shall dwell among you. I am not like a human being who abhors to dwell in one place. Furthermore, when you go into the land of your enemies and the temple is no longer among you, My glory shall go with you. Note, I shall be your Elokim. You shall be My people, for I took you out of the land of Mitzrayim for that purpose.

And I have broken the bars of your yoke. Scripture employs the metaphor of a plowing bullock that works the land of its owner, for Yisrael was forced to work as slaves in improving the land. The latter is clearly stated.
Upright. Kommemiyyut means upright.

The empty heads say that there are more curses than blessings. However, they do not speak the truth. What Scripture does is to speak of the blessings in general terms. However, it lists the curses in detail in order to frighten and scare the listeners. What I say will be clear to the one who reads the text carefully.
All these commandments. These that are written.
But break. The word le-hafrekhem (but break) is grammatically irregular, for the forms of verbs change.
And I will appoint…over you. As one who is appointed over another does whatever he wants, to him.
Terror…even consumption and fever. Common diseases. The meaning of et (even) is “with”.

The meaning of behalah (terror) is that you will be terrified and will not know what to do. There are those who say that behalah (terror) means suddenly. Many say that shachefet (consumption) and kadachat (fever) are diseases of the seed like blasting and mildew, for Scripture clearly states that the latter are such diseases (Amos 4:9). They say this because our verse states, and ye shall sow your seed in vain. However, there is no need for this, for the meaning of our verse is that they shall be struck with illnesses and if marauders shall come to the villages they shall then eat their seed, for there will not be anyone to go out and scatter the raiders.

The meaning of that shall make the eyes to fail is that these diseases will darken the eyes and languish the soul. The alef is missing in the word medivot (languish) in and the soul to languish. It is similarly missing in the word mezin (giveth ear) in And a liar giveth ear (Prov.17:4). Some say that the eyes to fail speaks of the eyes of the body because it goes on to say and the soul to languish. However, there is no need for this interpretation.

And I will set my face against you. My wrath and My anger. Compare, and her countenance was no more (Shmuel I 1:18). The meaning of our verse is that those that remain and are not stricken by disease will be smitten before their enemies, should they go out to fight them. At other times they will flee when no one pursues them as in the case of the Arami camp.
And if ye will not yet for these things. The plagues.
