Seven. The number seven is used for “many” because it is a complete number. Similarly, For a righteous man falleth seven times (Mishlei 24:16); While the barren hath born seven (Shmuel I 2:5). Al chatatekhem (for your sins) does not add the number seven to each sin. Its meaning is, I will punish you again for each sin. Ve-yasafti (then …more) is similar to yasaf (more) in and it went on no more (Devarim 5:19).

The meaning of al chatatekhem is, because of your sins. Some say that the number seven is to be taken literally. However, the first interpretation is correct, for if we count And I will break…(v. 19) as one; your heaven as iron (v. 19) as two; and your earth as brass (v. 19); And your strength shall be spent in vain (v. 20); for your land…her produce (v. 20); the trees of the land…their fruit (v. 20), then we have six. Note, the plague of beast of the field (v. 22) makes seven.
The pride of your power. The satiated, as in But Yeshurun waxed fat, and kicked (Devarim 32:15). When the proud are broken they fall and are brought low.
And your strength shall be spent in vain. The strength which you expended in working the soil.

Contrary. Many say that the meaning of keri (contrary) is power and might. You will act like a person who hardens his heart and is not afraid that he will be defeated. The word keri has no neighbor. Other say that the word keri is related to korot (befallen) in all that had befallen (Bereshit 42:29). Its meaning is found in what Scripture says in the account of the Plishtim wherein we read, it is not His hand that smote us; it was a chance (mikreh) that happened to us (Shmuel I 6:9). According to both interpretations the word keri is missing a bet. It is like the word sheshet (six) in for in six days (Shemot 20:11). Or, ve-im telekhu immi keri (and if you walk contrary unto Me) is to be read as if written ve-im telekhu immi halikhat keri (if you walk, a contrary walk, unto Me). I have already shown you many such instances. Note, our verse reads according to your sins. God will not add to the sins. Al chatatekhem (for your sins) (v. 18) is connected to le-yasserah etkhem (chastise you). The meaning of al chatatekhem (for your sins) is because of your sins.
And I will send…among you. Ve-hishlakhti (and I will send) is related to the word mashli’ach (send) in behold, I will send (Ex.8: 17).
Which shall rob you of your children. By killing your little ones.
And make you few in number. By the death of adults.
And your ways shall become desolate. For there will be no way that will be secure from the fear of wild animals. I have previously explained this.
Ye will not be corrected. Tivvaseru (be corrected) is a nifal imperfect.
For your sins. Al chatatekhem (for your sins) is connected to ve-hikketi (and I will smite).

The vengeance of the covenant. Our verse mentions the covenant. On the basis of this I earlier said that our Torah portion contains the covenant referred to in the Torah reading Now these are the ordinances (Shemot 21:1). The covenant was made on the day Yisrael promised [All that the Lord hath spoken ] will we do, and obey (Shemot 24:7). The covenant was then made and Moshe told them this portion.

And ye shall be gathered together within your cities. Because of the sword. There I will send the pestilence and the famine. The pestilence and the famine will cause you to desire to be delivered into the hand of the enemy. This is the meaning of and ye shall be delivered into the hand of the enemy. Ve-nittattem (and ye shall be delivered) is a nifal.

When I break. Shivri (I break) is an infinitive. It is vocalized with a chirik. Compare, shikhvah (she lay down) in when she lay down, nor when she arose (Bereshit 19:33). The Torah employs the term break because it speaks of the staff of bread. The latter is a metaphor. We find that Yeshayahu employs the phrase stay of bread (Is.3:1), for bread stays man’s heart (Tehillim 104:15).

Ten women. Scripture says ten women, for ten is the last of the numbers. It was the custom of Yisrael for each family to bake one oven full of bread for them to eat for the entire week. The arrangement of the Sabbath bread is proof of this.
And they shall deliver your bread again by weight. For it will consist of a small amount.
And ye shall eat, and not be satisfied. There are hungry people who are satisfied by eating a little amount of food. However, you will not be satisfied from eating much food.
And…for all this. By being smitten by this plague. And if in…these things (v. 23) similarly means, and if because of the previously mentioned plagues.
For your sins. This is connected to and I also will chastise you.
And ye shall eat the flesh of your sons… There is no famine worse than this one.
You will not have a place to cry out and pray to be saved from the famine, for I will destroy your high places, the place of the sacrifices.

Your sun-pillars. Chammnekhem is related to the word chammah (sun). Chammnekhem refers to structures built for the purpose of bowing down to the sun. The nun of chammnekhem is superfluous. It is like the nun of rachamaniyyot (compassion) in women full of compassion (Eichah 4:10).

Your carcasses. Pigrekhem means your carcasses. Compare, As a carcass (peger) trodden under foot (Is. 14:19). YOUR IDOLS. Gillulekhem (your idols) is a disparaging term for idols. Gillulekhem is related to the word galal (dung) in sweepeth away dung (Melachim I 14:10). The meaning of our verse is that when Yisrael joins themselves to temples dedicated to idol worship they will be killed there and their enemies will destroy the images of their idols. I (God) will not help them.
And my soul shall abhor you. The divine presence shall be removed.
and your cities will then be destroyed and your sanctuaries desolated. Your sanctuaries (v. 31) refers to the temples, which were at first My (God’s) sanctuaries.

And I will not smell the savor of your sweet odors. Scripture states this for the heaven and earth are full of Hashem’s glory. Scripture writes with regard to Noach, And Hashem smelled the sweet savor (Bereshit 8:3). Its meaning is, I will not accept a burnt offering from you after this.
After stating your cities and your sanctuaries, Scripture mentions the land. The reference is to all of the Land of Yisrael.
Shall be astonished at it. There will be so much destruction that the enemies who dwell there will also be astonished. Our verse is in contrast to The joy of the whole earth (Eichah 2:15).
Will I scatter. Ezareh (will I scatter) is a pi’el. Not only will you be scattered but I will also draw out the sword after you.
The meaning of draw out is draw out from its sheath.
And your land. This is connected to the verse which follows it. Its meaning is, when your land shall be desolate it will then be paid for its Sabbaths.
The word tirtzeh means pay. Compare, Till he shall accomplish (yirtzeh), as a hireling, his day (Iyov 14:6); That her guilt is paid off (nirtzah) (Is. 40:2).
Her sabbaths. Sabbatical years and Jubilees. It is similarly written, until the land had been paid her sabbaths (Divrei Hayamim II 36:21). I have explained it there.
Desolate. Hashammah (desolate) is a noun. The forms of the nouns change.

The meaning of as long as it lieth desolate, and ye are in your enemies’ land is that the land will be desolate, for you will not inhabit it. Then the land will not be worked and it will find rest and complete its Sabbaths.
[35. As long as it lieth desolate.] The meaning of as long as it lieth desolate is, the number of years that it shall not be worked. This is explained in Yechezkel.
And as for them that are left of you. Scripture says this because it previously stated, and I will draw out the sword after you (v. 33).

A faintness. Morekh (faintness) comes from a double root. Similarly, the word mo’al (lifting up) in with the lifting up of their hands (Nechemyah 8:6). The word morekh is related to the word rakh (faint) in and faint-hearted (Devarim 20:8). They will be so scared that the sound of a driven leaf shall chase them. Niddaf (driven) is an adjective in the nifal. The root nun is swallowed.
One upon another. Whom he loves.
To stand. Tekumah (stand) is a hifil. It comes from a root whose middle root letter is a vav. The aforementioned is so because of the tav. It is the same case with the word terumah (offering).
Shall eat you up. It is the norm for most of those exiled to other places to die because of the effect that the change in the air and the water has upon them.
And they that are left. And from those that are left.

[Shall pine away.] Yimmakku (shall pine away) follows the form of yissabbu (turned) in they turned not (Yechezkel 1:9). Both words come from a double root. Yimmakku is related to the word hamak (consume away) in Their flesh shall consume away (Zecharyah 14:12) and mak (rottenness) in there shall be rottenness (Is. 3:24).
And also in the iniquities of their fathers shall they pine away with them. Its meaning is like that of Our fathers have sinned (Eichah 5:7). I explained this in my commentary on Lamentations.
And they shall confess. Ve-hitvaddu (and they shall confess) is a hitpa’el.
In their treachery which they committed against me. Which their fathers committed against Me.
And also that they have walked contrary unto me. These, their children, have walked contrary unto Me.
I also. Did the same thing to them. I punished them by bringing them into the land of their enemies until their uncircumcised heart will be humbled. I will explain it later.
They then be paid the punishment of their iniquity. Yirtzu (be paid) means they will compensate and pay.

Then will I remember my covenant. My covenant is to be read as if written twice. Then will I remember My covenant with Yaakov is to be interpreted as if written, Then will I remember My covenant, My covenant with Yaakov. Compare, even the prophesy, Oded the prophet (Divrei Hayamim II 15:8), which is to be read as if written, even the prophesy, the prophesy of Oded the prophet; your heads, your tribes (Devarim 29:9), which is to be read as if written, your heads, the heads of your tribes. The Gaon says that the reason Scripture mentions Yaakov first is that all of his years were in the covenant.
For the land shall lie forsaken without them. This means I will also remember the land that paid off its Sabbaths and was forsaken without them. I will also remember that they paid for their sin.

Because, even because. The first because corresponds to they rejected Mine ordinances. The second one corresponds to and their soul abhorred My statutes. The bet of ve-ya’an (even because) is superfluous. It is like the bet of ba-rishonah (in the beginning) (Bereshit 13:4).

And yet for all that. Ve-af gam zot (and yet for all that) is an elegant phrase. One word would have sufficed. We find this in all of Scripture. Compare, ha-rak akh be-mosheh (hath indeed…only with Moshe) (Bamidbar 12:2); ha-mibbeli en kevarim (because there were no graves) (Shemot 14:11).
I will not reject them…to destroy them utterly. But I will punish them until their hearts are humbled.
Neither will I abhor them. Ge’altim (will I abhor them) means I did not turn away from them. Or, it means I did not abhor them.
To break my covenant. Which I made with them by oath. Even though, as Scripture states, they broke My covenant, I will not break My covenant with them, for I am the Lord.
But I will for their sakes remember. Forever.

The covenant of their ancestors. The reference is to the covenant made at Sinai. Scripture refers to this generation as “the first,” in contrast to their descendants who will be exiled in the land of their enemies. Some say that the reference is to the “patriarchs of the world,” and the meaning of whom I brought forth is those to whom I swore that I would free their children from slavery. The first interpretation appears to me to be the correct one.

These are the statutes and ordinances. These statutes and ordinances are recorded in the Torah portion Now Yitro…heard (Shemot 18:1); Now these are the ordinances (Shemot 21:1), and In mount Sinai (Vayikra 25:1).

Which Hashem made between him and the children of Yisrael. This alludes to the covenant made at Sinai, for after the tabernacle was erected and the glory was present in the tent of meeting, Moshe did not ascend Mount Sinai. Scripture also mentions the section of valuations here because it was related to Moshe at Mount Sinai. The latter is clearly stated at the end of the portion. For the beginning of the Book of Bamidbar, And Hashem spoke unto Moshe in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting (Bamidbar 1:1), is similar to the opening of the Book of Vayikra.
Shall clearly utter. Yafli (clearly utter) means to explain and to clarify.

A vow of persons. Its meaning is, he will take a vow saying: If Hashem will do the following for me then I will redeem my life in accordance with its value, or the value of my son’s life, or the value of the life of a beast. The kaf of be-erkekha (according to thy evaluation) is, according to all of the grammarians, superfluous. However, there is one who says that the kaf is directed to the kohen. He explains ke-erkekha ha-kohen (v. 12) as, as thou the priest valuest it. He refers to the heh of ha-kohen as a vocative heh. He says that the word, he-erkekha (of thy valuation) (v. 23), is an irregular word. It is like the word ha-oholi (of my tent) in the midst of my tent (Yehoshua 7:21). However, in my opinion the meaning of ha-oholi is, the tent, mine. Similarly he-erkekha (of thy valuation) (v. 23).
Nefashot (persons) takes in both men and beasts.
From twenty years old. Starting when one reaches the age of those who are counted [to go out to war].

Sixty years old. Old age. According to many, it is the decree of the King that from a month until five years he shall give five shekalim; that is, if the child is a day past a month, the one who vowed shall give five shekalim (v. 6). However, according to the Gaon, he shall give a shekel per year until five full years have passed. Many say that these are four valuations corresponding to four divisions of life. Next comes nineteen complete years. Then comes fifty-nine years when one is valued at the amount he started with. The fifteen are for the completion of seventy-five years corresponding to the four parts. However, in truth, they are all complete years. Or, one day in the year is considered a year. We will only rely on the words of tradition. For what reason is there to differentiate between a month until five, and from five until twenty since he gives a shekel for each year? We can refute the latter from the law regarding a child of a month. Note, one who is less than a month old has no value. After the age of sixty one goes backwards. Furthermore, what should one do after sixty? Shall he always give the same? These are all errors. The general rule is that it is a Scriptural decree. If the amount to be given in valuation was based on the additional shekalim above which the male is valued over the female, then note that after the age of sixty a third is added. From five to twenty add a half, and from the age of a month until five and from twenty until sixty one adds to the half its tenth.

And the priest shall value him. He shall be assessed in one evaluation based on every object that he owns. The word arokh (compared) in none to be compared unto Thee (Tehillim 40:6) is similar to he’erikh (value him). He’erikh is a hifil. Similarly ya’arikhennu (value him) in shall the priest value him? He’erikh is to be distinguished from ya’arkhennu (he shall set it in order) in he shall set it in order before Hashem (Vayikra 24:8).

[Then he shall be set. ] The kohen. Our verse should be interpreted as if written; and the kohen shall set him before the kohen. It is similar to my interpretation of and pour it into the palm of his own left hand (Vayikra 14:15). Ve-he’emido li-fene ha-kohen (then he shall be set before the priest) is lyrical. On the other hand, then he shall be set might mean that the one who vows shall set him.
So shall it stand. Yakum means so shall it stand.
And if…his possession. Which he inherited with the nation of Yisrael.

A homer of barley. Scripture writes, for ten baths are a homer (Yechezkel 45:14). Scripture there writes, The ephah and the bath (Yechezkel 45:11). Note, the sowing of an ephah of barley is valued at five shekalim. This is a decree of the King regarding the monetary value of a slave.
If…from the year of jubilee. In that very year.
And an abatement shall be made from thy valuation. The time that passed since the Jubilee.

[And if he…will indeed redeem.] The vav of ve-im ga’al yigal (and if he…will indeed redeem) is like the Arabic fa. It is connected in meaning to the verses that are above for the valuation is the main thing. Its meaning is, if he redeems the field or if he does not redeem it.
Or if he have sold. Ve-im makhar means, or if he have sold. The owner of the field cannot redeem the field because he sold it. It is to be holy to Hashem.
When it goeth out in the jubilee. Scripture employs the same language as it does with regard to all fields, for it goes out in the Jubilee.
As a field devoted. It belongs to the kohen as a field does which one takes a vow to devote. The amount of the valuation is the kohen’s, for he assesses it. He does not have to be a kohen gadol.
Thy valuation. Mikhsat (the worth of) is similar to mikhsat (number of) in according to the number of (Shemot 12:4).
Of whom it was bought. The reference is to the seller. This is explained by to whom the possession of the land belongeth.

Which is born as a firstling to Hashem. Known to be Hashem’s. Yevukkar (which is born as a firstling) is a pu’al. No man shall sanctify it by saying, “I will give the first-born to Hashem.” This is its meaning.

And if it be of an unclean beast. The first-born, along with the addition of a fifth of its value because he sanctified it. He shall also give a lamb, for Scripture so writes. If he does not sanctify the first-born, it may be sold. The first-born of an ass shall be exchanged in accordance with its valuation. He shall similarly give the sheep. Many say that it is not so.
Of all that he hath. Which is in his control.
Of man. Compare, I will devote (ve-hacharamti) their cities (Bamidbar 21:2).
[Be put to death.] The word yochoram (shall be devoted) is a hofal. Compare, yo’omad (shall be set) in shall be set alive (Vayikra 16:10).

Under the rod. The shepherd’s rod. Now the number one is the chosen one. The tenth is the same as the first. However, he may redeem the tenth. This is not the case with the first-born. Note, the Yisraeli shall give the first-born and the tenth of the beast, and of the seed of the ground, namely, of the produce, the first fruits and the tithe.
He shall not inquire. Yavakker (he shall…inquire) means he shall separate. I have previously explained that the word yavakker is related to the word boker (morning).

In Mount Sinai. I have explained this earlier in this Torah portion. The person who has the intelligence to understand the secret of the world will understand the secret of the first-born and the tenth. Now Avraham gave a tithe. Our father Yaakov, unto him the peace, did the same. If the One who has no second will help me, then I will reveal part of the secret when I mention the second tithe. The Book of Vayikra is completed.
